37.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Listen, listen, you who are held by desire: why do you go about swinging your arms (without a care)? You do not recognise your Husband; what face will you show when you go (to him)? The friends who have recognised the Husband: I fall at their feet. May I become just like them, joined in the union of the Sat Sangat. O young bride, the one who clings to falsehood is plundered by falsehood itself. The Husband, God, true and beautiful, is found through the understanding the Guru gives. The manmukh bride does not recognise the Husband; how will the night (of life) pass for such as her? Brimming with pride, they burn in craving and suffer pain in the love of another. The happy soul-brides steeped in the Shabad: Haumai departs from within them. They ever enjoy their Husband; their (night) passes in peace upon peace. Devoid of wisdom, the bride is cast off by her Husband; his love cannot be won (by her). In an ignorant mind there is darkness; without seeing the Husband, (her) hunger does not go. Come and meet me, my friends, and unite me with my Husband. By perfect fortune the True Guru is met; (then) the Husband is found, and (she) merges in the True One. Those friends are the happy soul-brides on whom he casts his glance of grace. Placing body and mind before him, they recognise their Master. She who drives out Haumai has found her Husband in her own home. O Nanak, those happy soul-brides are glorious; (each of them) is given to devotion night and day. ॥4॥
38.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Some (brides) enjoy their Husband; at whose door shall I go and ask (the way)? I serve the True Guru with love (and pray): unite me with my Husband. He himself creates all and watches over all; to whom is he near, from whom is he far? She who has known the Husband to be with her enjoys the Husband, ever present. O young bride, walk in the Guru's love. (So) night and day you will enjoy your Husband, merged in the True One in Sahaj. The happy soul-brides steeped in the Shabad are adorned with the true Shabad. In love and affection for the Guru, they find the Lord as Husband in their own home. Their bed is lovely, and the Lord delights there in love; their storehouses are full of devotion. That beloved God, who gives support to every one, dwells in their minds. Those who praise their Husband: I am ever a sacrifice to them. I offer (them) mind and body, give my head, and fall at their feet, theirs who have recognised the One, having cast off the love of another. O Nanak, through the Guru the Naam is recognised, and (one) merges in the True One. ॥3॥
38.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O Lord, you are true, the True One indeed; everything is in your power. Without meeting the Guru, the Pir, the beings of the eighty-four lakh forms of life wander in longing. Whom the dear Lord blesses and forgives, (that one's) body is ever at peace. By the Guru's grace, may I serve the True One, deep and profound. O my mind, when one is steeped in the Naam, there is peace. Through the Guru's teaching, praise the Naam; there is no other, no second. Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) has this command: sit and weigh true justice. The wicked soul in the love of another: that one is your subject. In the minds of the spiritual dwells the Lord, the treasure of virtues; they repeat (the Name of) the one Murari. Dharam Raj serves them; blessed is the One who adorns (them). One who casts the mind's vices out of the mind, from whose mind attachment and pride are gone, has recognised the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram), and in Sahaj is absorbed in the Naam. Without the True Guru liberation is not found; the manmukh wanders about like one insane. He does not recognise the Shabad; he only talks and talks, and stays sunk in Maya's poison. Everything is he himself; there is no other, no second. As he makes us speak, so we speak, when he himself makes us speak. The Bani of the Gurmukh is Brahm (God himself); through the Shabad comes union (with him). O Nanak, keep the Naam in your heart; by serving it there is peace. ॥4॥
39.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through the filth of Haumai the world has suffered pain; this filth has clung to it through the love of another. The filth of Haumai does not come off by any washing, even if one bathes at a hundred places of pilgrimage. People perform rites of many kinds, (but) twice the filth comes to cling to them. By reading, (too,) the filth does not come off; go and ask the learned. O my mind, when (one) comes to the Guru's refuge, then (one) becomes pure. The manmukhs have grown weary saying Har Har, yet the filth could not be washed away. With a filthy mind devotion cannot be done, and the Naam cannot be obtained. The manmukhs are filthy, have died filthy, and will depart having lost their honour. By the Guru's grace (the Lord) dwells in the mind, and the filth of Haumai is dissolved and gone. As a lamp lit in the dark (ends the darkness), so through the Guru's wisdom ignorance is driven out. We did (this), we shall do (that): (saying so,) we are foolish and ignorant. We have forgotten the Doer; (our) love is for another. There is no pain as great as Maya; all have wandered the world over (after it) and grown weary. Through the Guru's teaching, enshrining the True Name in the heart, peace is found. The one whom (the Lord) unites, he alone meets (him); I am a sacrifice to that one. O mind, for those steeped in devotion, the True One is their speech, and they find their own true home. Their minds are steeped, their tongues are steeped, and they sing the virtues of the True Lord. O Nanak, (they) do not forget the Naam, and they stay absorbed in the True One. ॥4॥
39.2: Sri Raag, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). In my mind and body is the very great pain of separation; how may the Beloved come to my home and meet me? When I see my God, at the sight of God the pain departs. I go and ask those friends: in what way is God met, how is the union brought about? O my True Guru, I have no other but you. We are foolish and ignorant, and have come to your refuge; may that Lord, in his mercy, unite (us with him). The True Guru is the giver of the Lord's Name; that God himself unites (one with him). The True Guru has come to know the Lord God; none other is as great as the Guru. Let me fall down in surrender at the Guru's refuge; in his kindness that God unites (one with him). By the stubborn force of the mind no one has found (him); everyone has tried every means and grown weary. (People) have tried a thousand clevernesses and given up; on a raw mind the dye (of love) does not take. By falsehood and deceit no one has found (him); whatever one sows, that one eats. All rest their hope in you, God; all beings are yours, and you are their wealth. God, no one goes away empty from you; at (your) door the Gurmukhs are acclaimed. Pull out those drowning in the poison of the terrifying world-ocean: this is the prayer of your servant Nanak. ॥4॥
40.1: Sri Raag, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). When the Naam is found, the mind is satisfied; cursed is life without the Naam. If some Gurmukh friend were to meet me and show me God, the treasure of virtues, I would be cut into four pieces as a sacrifice to the one who makes the light of the Naam shine in me. O my Beloved, I live by meditating on the Naam. Without the Name there is no life; O my True Guru, make the Naam firm within me. The Naam is a jewel beyond price; it lies with the perfect True Guru. When one takes up the True Guru's service, (the Guru) brings out the jewel and gives it, bringing light. Blessed are the fortunate, the most fortunate, who come and meet the Guru. Those who have not met the True Guru, the Being (Purakh), are luckless and in the power of Death. They are made to wander through births again and again, and are made hideous in filth. Let us not go anywhere near those within whom is vile anger. The True Guru, the Being, is the pool of Amrit; the fortunate come and bathe in it. The filth of their many births is washed away, (as the Guru) makes the pure Naam firm (within them). O servant Nanak, (they) have attained the highest state, fixing their attention on the True Guru. ॥4॥
40.2: Sri Raag, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Let me sing (his) virtues, unfold (his) virtues, speak (his) virtues, O my mother. The Gurmukh friend is the one who brings forth virtue; meeting that friend, one sings the Lord's virtues. The diamond (of the mind), meeting the Diamond (the Guru), has been pierced through, (and is dyed) deep red through the Name. O my Govind, as I sing (your) virtues, my mind is satisfied. Within (me) is thirst for the Lord's Name; the Guru, pleased, brings (one) to meet him. Dye your minds, O fortunate ones; the Guru, pleased, bestows his grace. The Guru makes the Naam firm (within) with love; to the True Guru I am a sacrifice. Without the True Guru the Lord's Name is not found, though I perform hundreds of thousands, millions of deeds. Without good fortune the True Guru is not met, though (he) is ever near, beside us as we sit at home. Within are ignorance, pain and doubt; with a veil between, distance has come to lie (between them). Without meeting the True Guru, (one) does not become gold; the manmukh, (like) iron, has sunk though the boat was beside him. The True Guru is the ship of the Lord's Name; in what way is it boarded? Whoever walks in the True Guru's will has come and taken a seat in the ship. Blessed, blessed and most fortunate are they, O Nanak, whom the True Guru unites (with the Lord). ॥4॥
41.1: Sri Raag, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Day after day I stand asking the way; if someone would tell me of God, I would go (to him) through that one. Those who have enjoyed my Beloved: let me follow behind them. Let me plead with them and implore them; I long to meet God. O my brothers, may someone unite me with the Lord God. To the True Guru I am a sacrifice: he has shown me the Lord God. Becoming humble, let me fall down before the perfect True Guru. To those without honour the Guru is honour; the Guru, the True Guru, gives (them) acclaim. Praising the Guru, I never have my fill; (he) unites me with the Lord God, near at hand. Everyone longs for the True Guru, the whole world, every one. Without good fortune the sight (of him) is not granted; the luckless one sits and weeps. What pleased the Lord God, that has come to be; what is written from the start no one can erase. He himself is the True Guru, he himself the Lord, and he himself unites (us) in union. He himself, showing mercy, will unite (us with him), placing (us) in the following of the Guru, the True Guru. The Life of the world is himself everywhere in the world; O Nanak, water merges in water. ॥4॥
41.2: Sri Raag, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Naam is an essence of Amrit, an essence exceedingly good; in what way may it be found, so that this essence can be tasted? Go and ask the sohaganis (the soul-brides united with their Husband Lord): how did God come and meet you? They, free of all care, say nothing; I rub and rub their feet and wash them. O brother, meeting the Friend (the Guru), keep the Lord's virtues in your heart. That Friend is the True Guru, the Purakh (the Being one with God), who slays Haumai and drives out pain. Those soul-brides who are Gurmukh were moved to compassion in their minds (and told me): The True Guru's word is a jewel; whoever accepts it tastes the Lord's sweet essence. Those who have tasted the Lord's sweet essence in love for the Guru are known as the fortunate ones, the great. This sweet essence of the Lord is in the forest, in every blade of grass, everywhere; but the unfortunate one does not taste it. Without the True Guru it does not come into one's grasp, and the manmukhs are left wailing. Before the True Guru they will not bow; within them dwells anger, a scourge. The Lord, Har Har Har, is himself the sweet essence; he himself becomes the Lord's essence. In his mercy he himself will give it: through the Guru the Amrit trickles down (within). O Nanak, the one in whose mind that Lord has come to dwell: (that one's) whole body and mind have turned green. ॥4॥
41.3: Sri Raag, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The day rises and then sets; the whole night, too, goes by. Life wears away, yet man does not understand; day after day the mouse (of time) gnaws at the rope (of life). Maya is spread out like sweet molasses; clinging to it like a fly, the manmukh is ruined and wastes away. O brother, that God alone is my friend and companion. Attachment to son and wife is poison; at the end no one stands by as a friend. Those who, by the Guru's teaching, fix their love on the Lord are saved; in (his) refuge they stay untouched (by Maya). They always kept their departure in view; they took the Lord('s Name) as provision for the road, and won honour. Through the Guru they are accepted in the Lord's court; the Lord himself clasps them to his heart. To the Gurmukhs the path lies plain; at the Lord's door no one bars their way. They praise the Lord's Name, the Name is in their minds, and they stay absorbed in the Name with loving attention. At their door (within), the unstruck melodies play, and at the True One's door they win glory. Those who, through the Guru, have praised the Name are hailed by everyone. O God, bless me with their company: this is my prayer, a beggar's prayer. O Nanak, those Gurmukhs have great fortune within whom the Naam shines forth. ॥4॥
42.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Why are you so absorbed, gazing at your sons and at your wife in her finery? You savour pleasures, make merry, and revel in endless delights. You give orders in plenty, and carry yourself puffed up with pride. The Creator does not come to your mind, O blind, foolish manmukh. O my mind, the giver of peace is that Lord alone. He is found by the Guru's grace; he is attained through (his) mercy. You are wrapped up in clothes and in the pleasures of food; gold, silver and land, fine horses and elephants of many colours, and chariots that never tire, you have gathered. You give no one a place in your thoughts; you have forgotten all your kin. The Creator has led you astray; without the Name you are impure. You take on the curses (of people) and pile up Maya (wealth). The one you seek to please (with it) is perishable, and so are you. O proud one, you are full of pride, gripped by your own mind's counsel. The one whom God himself has led astray has neither caste nor honour (that counts). Whom the True Guru, the Purakh, has united with that one Friend, that servant of the Lord has the One as his protector; what can mere men do (to him)? It is the one in Haumai who weeps. Whatever pleases the Lord's servant, (the Lord) does; at his door no one can turn it back. O Nanak, one dyed in the Lord's love becomes a light for the whole world. ॥4॥
42.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Though) the mind hold pleasures and revels of many kinds, and the eyes stay lost in delights, and kingdoms under royal canopies be one's own, (all these) lie steeped in anxiety. O brother, it is in the Saadh Sangat that peace has been found. (The one for whom) the Purakh, the Maker of destiny, wrote this lot: pain and anxiety have been wiped away. (One may have) roamed through every place there is in the world, and be a man of wealth and a great landlord, yet he lies sunk in crying mine, mine. One may issue commands without a qualm and act puffed up with pride, and may have brought everyone under his sway; yet without the Name he is mixed with the dust. (Though) the thirty-three crore (gods) be one's servants, and Siddhas and seekers stand at one's door, and one have heavy-laden riches and vast lordship, O Nanak, all of it turns into a dream. ॥4॥
Thirty-three crore (330 million): the number of the gods in Puranic tradition. Saadhik (seekers): those striving for the perfection of the Siddhas.
43.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Each morning on rising, (this body) is pampered, foolish and ignorant, without understanding. That God (who made it) has not come to mind; (at the end, this body) will be left behind in the wilderness. Fix your mind on the True Guru, and delight in bliss for ever and ever. O mortal, you have come (into the world) to gather profit. What worthless pursuits have you taken up? The whole night (of your life) is running out. Beasts and birds frisk and play; death is not in their sight. Man too is of their company, caught in the net of Maya. They alone are found free who keep the True Name cherished (in the heart). The house you must leave and lose has taken hold of your mind; where you must go and dwell, of that you take no thought. Of those ensnared, they alone get free who fall at the Guru's feet. No one (else) can save; no other is to be seen. Having searched in all four directions, I have come and fallen into (the Guru's) refuge. Nanak was drowning, and the True King has pulled him out. ॥4॥
43.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). A guest for a ghari or a muhat (a brief while), he sets himself up to put (this world's) affairs in order. Caught up in Maya and lust, the fool does not understand. When he rose and departed, he repented, and fell into the power of the cruel Jam. O blind one, you are sitting close by the (river's) bank. If it is so written from the beginning, then you will live by the Guru's word. It is not that the green crop is spared, nor the half-ripe, and only the ripe is reaped: sickles in hand, the reapers arrive, made ready (by the owner). When the farmer gave the order, they cut the whole field and measured it. The first watch went by in worldly tasks; in the second he slept his fill. In the third he wore himself out in futile pursuits; in the fourth the day broke. Never once did he call to mind the One who gave him soul and body. I am a sacrifice to the Saadh Sangat; I have given my soul in sacrifice to it, through which understanding has come into my mind, and I have met the all-wise Being. Nanak has seen the Lord, the knower of hearts, the wise, ever by his side. ॥4॥

A ghari is about twenty-four minutes, a muhat two gharis. In the harvest, the field is the world and the farmer God: at his order death takes the young, the grown and the old alike. Life is a night of four watches (pahar), and daybreak is death.
43.3: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Let all else be forgotten, but may the One never be forgotten. Burning away all my worldly entanglements, the Guru has given me the Name, the true aim (of life). Casting off all other hopes, I live by the hope of the One. Those who have served the True Guru have found a place hereafter. O my mind, sing the praises of the Creator. Give up all your clever ways and fall at the Guru's feet. Pain and hunger take no hold, if the giver of peace is in the mind. In no task does one suffer loss, when that True One is in the heart. The one you keep safe, (O God,) giving him your hand, no one can kill. Serve the Guru, the giver of peace: he washes away all faults and drives them out. Your servant, (O God,) begs to serve those whom you have set to your own service. The company of the holy and the toil (of service) I gain, O divine Lord, when you are pleased. Everything is in the Master's power; he himself does and causes all to be done. I am a sacrifice to the True Guru, who fulfils every wish of the mind. The One alone I see as my friend; the One alone is my brother and companion. All things belong to the One, and the order (of the world) is the One's. When the mind was won over by the One, the consciousness became steady. The True One is (his) food, the True One (his) clothing; Nanak has made the True One his support. ॥4॥
44.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). All things are gained, if the One comes into one's hands. This precious human birth bears fruit, if one speaks the True Shabad. Through the Guru, (the Lord's) mansion is attained by the one on whose forehead it is written. O my mind, fix your attention on the One. Without the One, all is entanglement; the love of Maya is all false. The joys of a hundred thousand kingdoms (are mine), if the True Guru casts his glance of grace. If he gives the Lord's Name for even an instant, my mind and body become cool and at peace. The one for whom it was so written from the beginning has grasped the True Guru's feet. Fruitful is the moment, fruitful the hour, in which there is love for the True One. Pain and torment do not touch the one whose support is the Lord's Name. The one whom the Guru has pulled out, holding him by the arm, he alone has crossed over. Beautiful and holy is the place where the Sants gather. Shelter is found only by the one who has found the Perfect Guru. O Nanak, (that one) has built a home where there is no death, no birth, no old age. ॥4॥
44.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my soul, meditate on him alone, the King over the heads of kings. O mind, place your hope in him alone, on whom all rely. Give up all your clever ways and fall at the Guru's feet. O my mind, repeat the Name in peace and Sahaj. At all hours meditate on God, and sing the praises of Govind every day. O mind, take refuge in him, to whom no other is equal in greatness; remembering whom brings abundant peace, and pain and sorrow do not come at all. Serve him for ever and ever: that God is the true Master. In the Saadh Sangat one becomes pure, and the noose of Jam is cut. He is the giver of peace and the destroyer of fears: offer your prayer before him. The one on whom the Merciful bestows mercy, his task is brought to fulfilment. He is called the greatest of the great; his abode is the highest of the high. He is beyond colour and form; I cannot tell his worth. Show mercy, God, and give Nanak your True Name. ॥4॥
44.3: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Whoever meditates on the Naam lives in peace, and his face is made radiant. (The Name) is received from the Perfect Guru, (and the one who receives it) is made known in all the worlds. The One, the True Lord, dwells in the home of the Saadh Sangat. Meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O my mind. The Naam is a helper, ever by your side, and hereafter it sets you free. Of what use are the honours of the world? All the pleasure of Maya is insipid; in the end it perishes. The one in whose heart the Lord dwells is perfect and foremost. Become the dust of the Saadh's feet, giving up your selfhood. Give up all schemes and cleverness, and cling to the Guru's feet. He alone obtains the jewel (of the Name) on whose forehead such fortune is written. O brothers, it comes only to the one to whom God himself gives it. He alone serves the True Guru whose fever of Haumai is destroyed. Nanak has met the Guru, and all his torments are gone. ॥4॥
45.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The One alone is the soul's intimate friend; the One alone is its protector. The mind's support is in the One alone; the One alone is the prop of the breath of life. In his refuge there is lasting peace; he is the Supreme Lord, the Creator. O my mind, abandon every (other) device. Worship the Perfect Guru every day, and keep your liv (loving attention) fixed on the One. The One alone is brother, the One the friend, the One alone mother and father. In the mind is the prop of the One who gave the soul and the body. May that God not slip from the mind, who has brought everything under his sway. In the home (the heart) is the One, outside is the One; in every place and every space between, he himself is present. He has made all beings and creatures: meditate on him at all hours. When one is imbued with the One, there is no grief and no anguish. The Supreme Lord God is One; there is no other. Soul and body, all is his; what pleases him is what comes to pass. Through the Perfect Guru one has become perfect, O Nanak, by meditating on that True One. ॥4॥
45.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those who have joined their mind to the True Guru are perfect and held in honour. Those to whom (God) himself is kind, in their mind spiritual wisdom wells up. Those on whose foreheads it was written (from the start) have obtained the Lord's Name. O my mind, meditate on the one Naam. (By it) the highest joys of all well up, and one goes to the Lord's court robed in honour. The fear of birth and death has gone, through loving devotion to Gopal (the Lord who sustains all). In the Saadh Sangat a person is made pure, and (God) himself keeps (him) safe. The filth of birth and death is cut away, and beholding the Guru one is filled with delight. That Supreme Lord God pervades every place and every space between. The Giver of all is One; there is no other. In his refuge one is set free; whatever he wishes to do, that comes to pass. Those in whose mind the Supreme Lord has come to dwell are perfect and held in honour. Their spotless glory has become known throughout the world. Those who have meditated on my God: Nanak is a sacrifice to them. ॥4॥
46.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Meeting the True Guru, all sorrow has gone, and the Lord's peace has come to dwell in the mind. Within, his Light has shone forth, through loving absorption in the One. Meeting the Saadh (the Guru), the face shines bright, and what was written from before is received. (Then) one sings Govind's praises every day, (joined) to the pure Name of the True One. O my mind, through the Guru's Shabad there is peace. No one who serves the Perfect Guru goes away empty-handed. The mind's desires are fulfilled; the treasure of the Naam has been found. The Knower of hearts is ever at (one's) side, and the Creator has become (one's) companion. By the Guru's grace the face shines bright, through meditating on the Naam, through giving and cleansing. Lust, anger and greed have perished, and all pride has been given up. The profit, the gain of the Naam, has been earned; the tasks are accomplished. In his grace God has united (one with himself) and given his own Name. Coming and going (in birth and death) has ended; (God) himself has become merciful. The true mansion, (one's own) home, has been found, and the Guru's Shabad has become (one's) companion. (God) protects his devotees, bestowing his grace. Here and hereafter their faces shine bright, as they cherish the virtues of the True One. At all hours they cherish (his) virtues, dyed in the love of the Infinite. The Supreme Lord is the ocean of peace; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥4॥
Naam, daan, isnaan: in Gurbani, meditating on the Naam, giving to others and pure living (cleansing) go together.
46.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). If the Perfect True Guru is met, the treasure of the Shabad is obtained. O God, show your grace, so that we may meditate on your Naam, the nectar of life; (so) the pain of birth and death is cut away, and attention rests in Sahaj. O my mind, come into God's refuge. Apart from the Lord there is no other; meditate on the one Naam. (His) worth cannot be told; he is an unfathomable ocean of virtues. O fortunate (mind), join the Sangat, and buy the True Shabad. Serve the Ocean of peace, the Emperor above the heads of kings. (I have) the support of (your) lotus feet; there is no other place. I have your support, O Supreme Lord; I live by your strength. O God, you are the honour of those without honour; may I stay merged in you. Let us meditate on the Lord, and worship Govind at all hours. (He) has kept safe the soul and the breath, the body and the wealth; in his grace he has saved the life. O Nanak, (he) has removed all faults; God, the Supreme Lord, is forgiving. ॥4॥
In the third stanza, ਰਹਾਉ is a verb, I remain, I live; it is not the shabad's Rahao (Pause).
46.3: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (My) love is fixed on that True One who neither dies nor comes and goes. Though one may try to part him, he does not part; he pervades all. The Destroyer of the pain and sorrow of the poor (is found) through the servant's sincere love. Wondrous is the form of the Niranjan (the One untouched by Maya); the Guru has united (me with him), O mother. O brother, make that God your friend. Cursed is the love of attachment to Maya; no one (in it) is seen at peace. He is all-knowing, the Giver, gracious in nature, pure, of boundless beauty. He is friend and helper, supremely great; lofty, great and boundless. He is known as neither child nor old; his court is unshakable. Whatever is asked (of him) is received; he is the support of the unsupported. Beholding him, sins are taken away, and mind and body grow still: let us meditate on that One with a single mind, casting off the mind's wandering. He is the treasure of virtues, ever new, and his giving is full. Let us worship him for ever and ever; do not forget (him), by day or by night. Those for whom it was written from before: Govind is their friend. Body, mind and wealth, all I offer (to him); this whole life is to be given up (for him). Ever present, he sees and hears; God pervades every heart. O God, you sustain even the ungrateful; says Nanak, you are ever forgiving. ॥4॥
47.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). God, who gave the mind, body and wealth and has kept them, finely fashioned, in Sahaj, who formed (the body) with every power, and set within it his boundless Light: let us remember that God for ever and ever; keep him within, enshrined in the heart. O my mind, apart from the Lord there is no other. Stay ever in God's refuge, and no pain will touch you. Jewels, precious things, rubies, gold and silver are (but) dust. Mother, father, sons, kinsfolk: all these ties are false. He does not know the One who made him: the manmukh is an unclean beast. The One who pervades within and without, him he thinks far away. Craving clings to him, he is engrossed (in Maya), and within him is false Haumai. Devoid of devotion and the Naam, they come and go in boatloads. Save (them), O God, Creator, showing mercy to (all) beings and creatures. Without God there is no one to protect; Jam has grown most dreadful. May Nanak not forget (your) Naam; O Lord, show your mercy. ॥4॥
47.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One says:) mine is this body and mine the wealth; mine the rule, the beauty and the land; sons, wives and many women, countless pleasures and robes. (But) if the Lord's Name does not dwell in the heart, count (all this) of no use at all. Meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O my mind. Keep the company of the Saadh (the Guru) every day, and fix your mind on the Guru's feet. The treasure of the Naam is meditated upon (when) good fortune is written on the forehead. All affairs are set right: hold fast to the Guru's feet. The disease of Haumai and doubt are cut away, and one neither comes nor goes. Keep the company of the Saadh: (that is) your bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage. Soul, breath, mind and body turn green (with life); this is the true aim (of life). Here you will receive honours, and in the Lord's court you will find a place. God himself does and causes all to be done; everything is in his hands alone. He himself kills and brings back to life; within and without he is with (all). Nanak has come into your refuge, O God, Master of all hearts. ॥4॥
48.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). They have come into the refuge of their God, those to whom the Guru has been kind; through the True Guru's teaching all their entanglements have been destroyed. Their inner being is attached to the Lord's Name, and by (his) nectar-filled glance they are filled with delight. O my mind, hold to the service of the True Guru. God shows his mercy; do not forget him from your mind for even an instant. Let Govind's praises be sung every day; they cut away faults. Without the Lord's Name there is no peace; the expanses (of Maya) have been tried and seen. Imbued in Sahaj with his praises, (they) have crossed the world-ocean. Pilgrimages, fasts and countless disciplines (are found) in gaining the dust of the Saadh's (the Guru's) feet. From whom does one hide what one does, when (God) sees, ever present? My God pervades, to the full, every place and every space between. True is his sovereignty, true his command; true is the True One's seat. He has set up a true creation (kudrat); the True One has fashioned the world. Says Nanak, let us meditate on the True Naam; I am a sacrifice (to him) for ever and ever. ॥4॥
48.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Make the effort and meditate on the Lord; O fortunate one, earn the wealth (of the Naam). In the company of the Sants remember the Lord, and cut away the filth of birth after birth. O my mind, repeat the Lord's Name, make it your chant. Enjoy the fruits your mind longs for, and all grief and anguish will end. The God for whose sake the body was taken on has been seen right at hand. God fills the water, the land and the sky, and watches over (all) with his glance of grace. Mind and body have become pure; love for the True One has taken hold. One who has worshipped the feet of the Supreme Lord has performed every chant and austerity. The Lord's Name, the nectar, is jewel, gem and ruby. (In it are) the delights of peace, poise and bliss; O servant Nanak, sing the Lord's praises. ॥4॥
48.3: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That alone is scripture (shastra), that alone the good omen, through which the Lord's Name is meditated upon. The Guru has given the wealth of (God's) lotus feet, and the one without a place has found a place. The true capital and the true self-discipline (is this): sing (his) praises at all hours. One whom God has met in his grace has no dying, no coming and going. O my mind, worship the Lord ever, dyed in the love of the One. He pervades within every heart, ever the helper, ever with (you). How can I count the measure of the joys, when I remember Govind? Those who have tasted (it) are satisfied; that soul (alone) knows the taste. In the company of the Sants, God, the beloved and forgiving, dwells in the mind. One who has served his own God, he alone is the king of kings. The moment in which the Lord's praise is sung and his virtues are dwelt upon holds millions of cleansing baths. The tongue that utters them is blessed with virtue; no gift of charity can equal it. Casting his glance (of grace), the kind and merciful Being comes to dwell in mind and body. Soul, body and wealth are his; I am a sacrifice (to him) for ever and ever. One who has been united is never again parted, when the Creator has united (him). The bonds of his servants have been cut by the True Creator. The one who had strayed he has set on the path, not weighing (his) merits and faults. Nanak is in the refuge of the One who is the support of all hearts. ॥4॥
The Shastras are the books of the six schools of Hindu philosophy; saun (shagun) is an omen, read as lucky or unlucky before an undertaking.
49.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Let us remember the True One with the tongue, and mind and body become pure. Mother, father and kin are many, but apart from him there is no other (lasting companion). If he shows his mercy, he is not forgotten for even a moment. O my mind, serve the True One for as long as there is breath. Apart from the True One, all is false; in the end it perishes. My Master is pure; without him I cannot live. In my mind and body there is a hunger (for him), very great; O mother, if only someone would bring (him) and unite me (with him). I have searched all four quarters; apart from the Husband Lord there is no other place (of refuge). Make your prayer before him (the Guru) who brings (you) to meet the Creator. It is the True Guru who gives the Naam, and his storehouse is full. Let us praise (God) for ever and ever, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore. Let us praise the Sustainer, whose wonders are many. Let us worship (him) in remembrance for ever and ever; this is the highest wisdom. O Nanak, he is sweet to the mind and body of that one alone on whose forehead (such) a destiny is written. ॥4॥
49.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Sants, brothers, come together and, keeping the True Name in your hearts, pack provisions (for the journey) of the soul, which stay with you here and hereafter. (This provision) is received from the Perfect Guru, when (God) looks on (one) with his gracious glance. By (his) grace it comes to the one on whom he is merciful. O my mind, none is as great as the Guru. I can see no other place (of refuge); it is that True One himself who unites (us) with the Guru. The one who has gone and beheld the Guru has received every treasure. Greatly fortunate, O mother, are those whose minds are fixed on the Guru's feet. The Guru is the Giver and the Guru is almighty; the Guru pervades all. The Guru is the Supreme God, the Supreme Lord; the Guru carries the drowning across. With what mouth can the Guru be praised? (He is) the Cause of creation, all-powerful. Those foreheads on which the Guru has placed his hand remain unshaken. The Guru has given (them) the nectar of the Naam to drink, the healing regimen against (the disease of) birth and death. They have served the Guru, the Supreme God, the destroyer of fear, the remover of pain. The True Guru is deep and profound, a sea of peace that wipes away sin. The one who has served his own Guru is not struck by the rod of Death's messengers. Nothing comes level with the Guru: I have searched the whole universe and seen. The one to whom the True Guru has given the treasure of the Naam, O Nanak, has set peace firmly in the mind. ॥4॥
ਪਥੁ (Sanskrit pathya) is the diet a physician prescribes for an illness; here the Naam is that regimen for the disease of birth and death.
50.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Taking (the world's pleasures) to be sweet, (the mortal) ate them, but a bitter taste came of them. He made brothers, friends and companions, and stirred up strife over the poison of Maya. (All these) pass away without delay; without the Name, (one is left) dumbfounded. O my mind, give yourself to serving the True Guru. All that is seen will perish; give up the counsel of your own mind. As a rabid dog runs off in all ten directions, (so) the greedy creature has no discernment: it devours everything, fit to eat or not. Gripped by the intoxication of lust and anger, (it) falls into birth after birth. Maya has spread out her net and set bait inside it. The bird, driven by craving, is caught (in it); O mother, it finds no way out. It does not know the One who made it, and comes and goes again and again. In countless ways and by many means this world is enticed. Only the one whom the all-powerful, infinite Being protects is spared. The Lord's servants have been saved through loving absorption in the Lord; Nanak is forever a sacrifice (to them). ॥4॥
50.2: Sri Raag, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The herdsman comes to the pasture (for a few days); what use to him are show and display? When the allotted time is over, he must go; look after your (true) home. Sing the Lord's praises, O mind, and serve the True Guru with love. Why take pride in a trifling thing? As guests for the night will rise and leave at daybreak, (so must you;) why are you absorbed in household life? All of it is (as brief as) a garden of flowers. Why do you keep saying mine, mine? Seek God, who gave (it all). One must surely rise and depart; (each one) will go, leaving lakhs and crores behind. After wandering through the eighty-four lakh forms of life, you have found this rare (human) birth. O Nanak, cherish the Naam; that day has drawn near. ॥4॥
A goil is grassland by a river where herders bring their cattle to graze for a few days in a dry season; their stay there is brief.
50.3: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O body, the bride,) you live at ease only as long as your companion (the soul) is with you. When the companion rises and departs, the bride is mixed into the dust. Detachment has arisen in the mind, and a longing to behold (your) sight. Blessed is that dwelling-place of yours. As long as the husband (the soul) dwells in the house, everyone addresses (you) as ji, ji. When the poor husband rises and leaves, no one will ask after you. (O soul-bride,) serve the Husband Lord in your parents' home (this world), and dwell in peace in your in-laws' home (the world hereafter). Meeting the Guru, learn the way to live and good conduct, and no pain will ever touch you. Everyone must go to the in-laws' home; all are to be sent off in the muklava. O Nanak, blessed are the happy brides who love their Husband. ॥4॥
In the first two stanzas the body is the bride and the soul her companion and husband; from the third, the soul is the bride and God the Husband.
The muklava is the rite by which a bride married young is later sent from her parents' home to her husband's.
51.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He alone, the One, is the Cause of creation, who made all (this visible) form. Meditate on him, O my mind: he is the prop of all. Dwell in meditation on the Guru's feet within your mind. Leave all cleverness aside, and through the Shabad attune yourself in love to the True One. Neither pain nor distress nor fear can seize the one in whose heart is the Guru's mantra. (People) have made millions of efforts and given up; without the Guru no one has crossed over. Beholding (the Guru), the mind finds its support, and every sin goes away. I am a sacrifice to those who throw themselves at the Guru's feet. In the Saadh Sangat, the Lord's True Name settles in the mind. Fortunate are they, O Nanak, in whose minds is this love. ॥4॥
51.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Amass the Lord's wealth, worship the True Guru, and abandon every vice. Remember the Lord who fashioned and adorned you, and you will be saved. O mind, repeat the Name of the One, the Infinite, who gave (you) the breath of life, mind and body, (and who is) the support of the heart. Drunk with lust, anger and ego, the world is in their grip. Seek the refuge of the Sant (the Guru), fall at (his) feet, and pain and darkness will be dispelled. (That one) practises truth, contentment and compassion, the most excellent of deeds; giving up self, he becomes the dust (of the feet) of all: the one to whom God, the Formless, gives (this gift). All that is seen is you, (O God); it is your own expanse spread out. Says Nanak, the Guru has cut away doubt; (now) God is contemplated in all. ॥4॥
51.3: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The whole world is caught up in (reckoning) bad deeds and good deeds. The devotee stands apart from both; rare is the one known to be such. The Master pervades all. What can I say, what can I hear (of you), my Lord? You are the great Being, the all-knowing. One who is caught up in honour and dishonour is not (God's) servant. O Sants, one who sees the Essence (God) and looks on all alike is one among millions. To talk (of wisdom) and have others talk: this is a road to renown. Rare is the Gurmukh who is free of speaking and telling. Liberation or bondage: nothing of these comes into the view of the one who, O Nanak, has received the gift of the dust of the Sants. ॥4॥
51.4: Sri Raag, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Relying on you, my Beloved, I have frolicked (as a cherished child). Children stray and make mistakes; O Lord, you are (our) father and mother. It is easy to say and to have it said, (but) hard to abide by your will. My pride is in you, my strength is yours; I know you as my own. You are within all and beyond all, O Father who depends on no one. Father, I do not know what your ways are. O Sants, (the Father) sets free from bonds, and he holds me as his own. The Master has become merciful; (my) coming and going is over. Meeting the Guru, Nanak has recognised the Supreme Lord. ॥4॥
52.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through meeting the Sants, the brothers, Jamkaal has been cut away. The True Master has come to dwell in the mind; the Lord and Master has become merciful. The Perfect True Guru has been met, and all the entanglement (of Maya) has been destroyed. O my True Guru, to you I am a sacrifice. To the sight of you I give myself in sacrifice; pleased, you have given (me) the nectar of the Naam. Those who have served you lovingly, they alone are wise. Following those within whom is the treasure of the Naam, one is set free. No giver is as great as the Guru, who has bestowed the gift of the spirit. Approved is the coming (into the world) of those who have met the Guru in love. Imbued with the True One, they find a place to sit in the Lord's court. Glories rest in the Creator's hands; (each one) receives as the writ of the past decrees. The True One is the Creator, the True One the Doer, the True One the Master, the True One the support. Let us call the True One alone true; the True One alone is discerning wisdom. He pervades all, within all, without a break; Nanak lives by repeating (the Name of) the One. ॥4॥
52.2: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Let us worship the Guru, the Supreme God, with love in mind and body. The True Guru gives the soul its life; he gives support to all. To live by the True Guru's words: this is true understanding. Without being steeped in the company of the Saadh (the Guru), all love of Maya is but ashes. O my friend, cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har. In the company of the Saadh (the Name) dwells in the mind, and (one's) labour comes to fruition. The Guru is all-powerful and infinite; by great good fortune is the Guru seen. The Guru is beyond the reach of the senses, and pure; none is as great as the Guru. The Guru is himself the Creator, the Guru the Doer; through the Guru, one gains true glory. Nothing lies outside the Guru; what the Guru wills to be done comes to be. The Guru is the place of pilgrimage, the Guru the Paarjat tree, the Guru fulfils the mind's desires. The Guru is the Giver, bestowing the Lord's Name, through which the whole world is delivered. The Guru is all-powerful, the Guru is the Formless One; the Guru is lofty, beyond reach and without limit. The Guru's glory is beyond reach; what can any teller tell? All the fruits the mind longs for are with the True Guru. They are received by the writ of the past; (the Guru) gives the capital of the True Name. For one who has come to the True Guru's refuge, there is no perishing again. O Lord, may Nanak never forget you; this soul, this body and this breath are yours. ॥4॥
The Paarjat (Parijata) is a tree of Indra's heaven which, in the Puranas, rose from the churning of the ocean and grants every wish.
52.3: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Sants, brothers, listen: release comes through the True Name. The Guru's feet are to be worshipped; the Lord's Name is the place of pilgrimage. Hereafter (such ones) are honoured in the Lord's court, and the shelterless find shelter. O brother, the service of the True Guru is true (and bears fruit). When the True Guru is pleased, the Perfect One, unseen and unfathomable, is found. I am a sacrifice to the True Guru, the one who gave the True Name. Night and day (my task) is to praise the True One; I sing the virtues of the True One. The True (Name) is (my) food, the True (Name) (my) clothing; (my support is) the True Name of the True One. Let him not be forgotten with any breath or morsel: the Guru himself is the embodiment that bears every fruit. No other is seen as great as the Guru; meditate on him at all hours. When he looks with grace, the True Name, the treasure of virtues, is received. The Guru and the Supreme God are one; he pervades all. Those whose writ of the past so decrees, they alone meditate on the Naam. O Nanak, one who has come to the Guru's refuge neither dies nor comes and goes. ॥4॥
53.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Sri Raag, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Uttering (his praise) again and again, one plays the mind like an instrument, and plays it as far as one comes to know how. The One for whom (the mind) is played and (the praise) is sung: how great is he, and in what place does he dwell? All those who speak of him, as many as they are, have spoken with their attention lovingly fixed, until they could go no further (and have not found his end). O brother, Allah (God) is beyond reach and without limit. Pure is his glory, and pure his dwelling-place; he is the True One, the Sustainer (of all). (O God,) how far your Hukam reaches is not known; no one can set it down in writing. If a hundred poets were brought together, for all their toil they could not reach (so much as) a sesame seed's worth of it. No one has found your worth; all only repeat the report (of you) that they have heard and heard (from others). Pirs, prophets, travellers on the path, men of faith, humble fakirs and martyrs, shaikhs, the elders among the shaikhs, qazis, mullas, and dervishes who have reached (his) door: (among them) abundant blessing is theirs who go on reciting the darood (prayers of praise) to him. He asks no one before he makes, asks no one before he pulls down, asks no one as he gives or takes away. His own creative power (Kudrat) he alone knows; he himself brings forth the creation. He looks after all with his glance of grace, and gives to whoever pleases him. The names of (all) the places (of his creation) cannot be known; how great, among all names, is his Name? How vast is the place where my King dwells? No one can reach (there); whom am I to go and ask? When he makes someone great, castes high or low count for nothing with him. Glory lies in the hands of the Great One; he gives to whoever pleases him. By his own Hukam he sets (a life) right, and does not delay even a moment. With the thought of receiving (from him), everyone says, (give me) much, still more. How great a Giver can he be called? He keeps on giving beyond all count. Says Nanak, (O God,) your storehouses, age after age, never run short. ॥7॥
Ashtapadi (ashta, eight; pad, stanza): a hymn of about eight stanzas.
Here ਨਾਈ is the Arabic sana, glory or praise (not ਨਾਉ, the Name); parvardigar (Persian) is the Sustainer.
Salik: one who travels the Sufi path; mashaikh: the great shaikhs (plural of shaikh); darood: the praise and blessing recited after the namaz.
53.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). All are the brides of the Husband (Lord), and all of them adorn themselves. (But those) who come to have their worth counted and shown, their bright red dress is a vice. Love is not won by hypocrisy; false show brings only ruin. O Lord, this is how the Husband takes delight in his bride: those who please you are the happy soul-brides; by your own grace you adorn them. She who is adorned with the Guru's Shabad has given her body and mind into her Husband's keeping. She stands with both hands joined, looking towards him, and speaks her prayer to the True One. Dyed in her Beloved, she dwells in the fear of the True One; steeped in love, she is immersed in his colour. She is called the Beloved's handmaid; that handmaid holds to (his) Name. Her true love does not break; in the True One's company her union (endures). Steeped in the Shabad, her mind is pierced through (with love); I am ever a sacrifice to her. That soul-bride never sits as a widow, if she merges in the True Guru. Her Husband is the home of all delight, ever new, true; he neither dies nor is born. With his true glance of grace, in his own will, he ever delights in the happy wife. The bride who dresses her hair with Truth, and makes love her clothing and her adornment, whose sandalwood is (the Lord) enshrined in her mind, and whose palace is the Tenth Gate, who has lit the lamp through the Shabad, and wears the Lord's Name as the necklace on her breast: she is beautiful among women; love is the jewel on her forehead. Her glory is her lovely awareness, (absorbed) in love of the True, the Infinite One. She knows no man but her Husband, (living) in love and affection for the True Guru. O you who lie asleep in the dark night, how will your night pass without the Husband? May that heart burn, may that body be burned, may mind and wealth burn away, when the Husband has not taken delight in his bride, then her youth goes to waste. The young bride lies asleep on her Husband's bed, yet does not understand. I am asleep and my Husband is awake; whom shall I go and ask? She whom the True Guru unites (with him) dwells in the fear (of God); O Nanak, love becomes her companion. ॥8॥
The Tenth Gate (dasam duar): the inner door beyond the body's nine openings, where the soul meets God.
54.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (God) himself is the virtues, he himself tells of them, and he himself hears and reflects on them. You yourself are the jewel, you yourself assay it, and you yourself are its boundless worth. You are the true honour and greatness, and you yourself are the one who bestows them. O Lord, you are the Maker, the Creator. Keep me as it pleases you; may I receive the Lord's Name, (and may that be) my way of life. You yourself are the flawless diamond, you yourself the (fast) colour of madder. You yourself are the shining pearl, you yourself the go-between for your devotees. Through the Guru's Shabad you are praised; in every heart you are the seen and the unseen. You yourself are the ocean and the ship; you yourself are the far shore and the near. You, the All-wise, are the true way, and through the Shabad you take (us) across. Those who do not fear (God) come to know fear; without the Guru there is pitch darkness. Only the Creator is seen to stand for ever; all else, however vast, comes and goes. You alone, the One, are pure; all others are caught and bound in worldly entanglements. Those whom the Guru has protected are saved, lovingly attuned to the True One. The Lord is recognised through the Shabad; through the Guru's word (beings) are steeped in the True One. No filth clings to the body of one whose dwelling is in the True One's home. When he casts his glance of grace, the True One is found; without the Name, what kinship (with him) can there be? Those who have recognised the True One are at peace through all four ages. Killing Haumai and craving, they have kept the True One enshrined in the heart. In the world the one profit is the Name, and it is gained by reflecting on the Guru's teaching. Let the true merchandise be loaded: the profit lasts for ever, and the capital is Truth. One whose devotion and prayer are true takes a seat in the True Court. His account is settled with honour, and the Lord's Name shines forth (within him). He is called the Highest of the high; I say it too, but (by saying) he cannot be seen. Wherever I look, there you alone are; the True Guru has shown (you to me). O Nanak, in Sahaj and in love, (God's) Light is known to pervade all without a break. ॥8॥
Majith (madder): a plant whose red dye never fades; in Gurbani, the image of lasting love.
55.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The fish of the deep salt sea did not know the net for what it was. So clever and so lovely, why did she put her trust (in it)? Because of what she did she was caught; death does not turn away from her head. O brother, know that death stands over your head in just this way. As on the fish, so on human beings the net (of death) falls unawares. All the world is held in death's bonds; without the Guru there is no turning death aside. Those steeped in the True One are saved, giving up double-mindedness and vice. I am a sacrifice to those who are found true at the door of the True One. As the hawk is to the birds, and the net in the hunter's hand, (so is death to all beings): Those whom the Guru has protected are saved; the rest are caught along with the bait. Without the Name they are singled out and cast away; no friend or companion stands with them. The True One alone is to be called true; true is the True One's dwelling. Those who have accepted the True One keep the True One in their minds' meditation. Those who, through the Guru, have the knowledge (of God) are known to be pure in mind and in mouth. Pray before the True Guru, and he unites (you) with the Friend. Meeting the Friend, peace is found; Death's messengers die, as if they had swallowed poison. I dwell within the Name, and the Name comes to dwell in my mind. Without the Guru there is pitch darkness; without the Shabad, understanding is not gained. Through the Guru's teaching there is light (within), and one stays lovingly attuned to the True One. Death does not move there; one's light merges in the Light. (O God,) you alone are the Friend, you the All-wise; you yourself are the one who unites. Through the Guru's Shabad you are to be praised; you have no end, no near or far shore. Death does not reach there, where the Guru's boundless Shabad abides. By (God's) Hukam all are born; by Hukam they do their work. By Hukam (the world) is in death's power; by Hukam (beings) merge in the True One. O Nanak, what pleases him, that alone happens; nothing is in the power of these beings. ॥8॥
55.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If the mind is impure, the body too is defiled, and the tongue becomes impure. A false mouth speaks only falsehood; how can such a one become pure? Without the water of the Shabad (the mind) is not scoured clean; truth comes from the True One alone. O young bride, what peace can there be for one without virtue? (The virtuous one) will enjoy the delights of union with her Husband in joy; peace lies in the true Shabad, in love. If the Husband goes to a far land, the bride left behind pines away, and like a fish in shallow water she cries out in piteous pleading. If she pleases her Husband, peace is found, when he himself casts his glance of grace. Join your friends and companions and praise your Husband. (Then) he shines within her body, her mind is enchanted, and, dyed in his love, she beholds him. Adorned by the Shabad she grows beautiful, and through her virtues she enjoys her Husband. The bride who is false and full of faults is of no use. She has no peace in her parents' home or in her in-laws'; she burns in falsehood and vice. Her coming and going (birth and death) are hard; her Husband has forgotten her and cast her off. She was her Husband's lovely bride; for what pleasure was she cast off? She is of no use to her Husband; she speaks idle, empty words. She finds no shelter at his gate or in his home; she is cast off for the taste of another (than him). Pandits read their books, but do not grasp their meaning. They give counsel to others and go their way; theirs is a trade in Maya. With false talk the world wanders; living by the Shabad, that is what is excellent. So many pandits and astrologers deliberate on the Vedas. In wrangling and controversy they win praise; in wrangling their coming and going goes on. Without the Guru's grace no one will be set free, by speaking, hearing, saying and expounding. All (the happy wives) are called virtuous; I have no virtue at all. The bride whose Husband is the Lord is beautiful; that God is dear to me (too). O Nanak, the union made through the Shabad knows no more parting. ॥8॥
56.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If chanting, austerity and self-restraint are practised, and one dwells at a place of pilgrimage, and works of merit, charity and good deeds are done, yet without the True One what are they worth? As one sows, so one reaps; without virtue, life is wasted. O young bride, as the handmaid of virtue you will find peace. Casting off faults, one merges (in him); through the Guru's teaching, that Perfect One (is found). A trader without capital looks this way and that, to all four quarters. He does not grasp his own source; the real goods lie (unnoticed) within his own house. Without the merchandise the suffering is great; the one who clings to falsehood is plundered by falsehood itself. Day and night there is ever-new profit for the one who assays the jewel (of the Name) with reflection. He finds the goods within his own home, and departs with his task accomplished, having traded with the traders (of the Name) and reflected on God through the Guru. The company of the Sants is found if the Uniter brings (one) to it. The one within whom is the infinite Light, once united, is never parted. On a true, unshaken seat he abides in the True One, loving the True One with deep affection. Those who have recognised themselves find (the Lord's) mansion within their own home, in a blessed place. Steeped in the True One, they gain the True One (as their own). Through the True Name, that God, the True One, is known (to pervade) the three worlds. That soul-bride is truly beautiful who has known her Husband to be with her. She, the bride of the palace, is called into the mansion, and the Husband delights in her with love. Absorbed in the True One, that happy soul-bride is good; the Husband has won her heart with (his) virtues. (If,) lost and astray, I climb the uplands, and from the uplands go on to the mountains, if I wander lost in the forest, without the Guru I gain no understanding. If I wander, strayed from the Name, I shall come and go again and again. Go and ask the travellers who have walked (the road) as his servants. They know the King as their own; at his gate and in his home no one bars their way. O Nanak, the One alone pervades all; there is no other, none at all. ॥8॥
57.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Through the Guru the Pure One is known, and body and frame are made pure. The Pure and True One comes to dwell in the mind, he who knows the pain within. From Sahaj comes great peace, and the arrow of Jam does not strike. O brother, bathing in the pure water (of the Name), no filth remains. You alone are pure and true, (O Lord); every other place is filled with filth. The Creator has made the Lord's temple beautiful. Sun and moon are its lamps of matchless light; the boundless Light (shines) through the three worlds. (In it are) shops, cities, forts and chambers, where the true merchandise is bought and traded. With the collyrium of wisdom, which destroys fear, behold the Stainless One in love. All that is hidden and all that is manifest is known, if one keeps the mind in its place. If such a True Guru is met, he unites (one with the Lord) in Sahaj. As (gold) is rubbed on the touchstone, (so the Lord) tests (us), with love and with full attention. The counterfeit find no place; the genuine are put into the treasury. Cast off hope and anxiety; in this way the filth departs and (one) merges (in the Lord). Everyone asks for pleasure; no one asks for pain. Yet in the wake of pleasure comes great pain; the manmukh does not understand this. When pleasure and pain are known as one, and (the mind) is pierced by the Shabad, there is peace. The Veda proclaims, and the word of Brahma and Vyas is read (to say), that the silent sages, the servants and the seekers are steeped in the Name of the treasure of virtues. Those steeped in the True One have departed victorious; I am ever a sacrifice to them. Those in whose mouth the Naam is not are filthy through the four ages, full of filth. Bereft of devotion and love, their faces are blackened and they lose their honour. Those who have forgotten the Naam are robbed by their failings and weep. Searching and searching, this is found: holding (God's) fear (in the heart), one is united (with him), brought together (by the Guru). One who recognises his own self dwells in his own home (within); Haumai and craving depart. O Nanak, those steeped in the Lord's Name are pure and radiant. ॥8॥
Brahma is the creator god of the Puranas, from whose mouths the Vedas are held to have come; Vyas is the sage held to have arranged the Vedas and composed the Puranas.
57.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Listen, O strayed and crazed mind: cling to the Guru's feet. Repeat the Lord's Name and meditate on it; Jam will be afraid, and sorrow will flee. Great is the pain of the forsaken soul-bride; how can her married happiness last? O brother, I have no other place. My wealth and treasure is the Naam; the Guru has given it, and I am a sacrifice (to him). Through the Guru's teaching honour is won; acclaim be to him (the Guru), and may I be joined to his company. Without him I cannot live a moment; without the Name I die. May I, the blind one, never forget the Naam; holding fast to (its) support, may I reach (my true) home. Those whose guru is (himself) blind: such disciples find no place of rest. The Name is not received without the True Guru; without the Name, what purpose (has life)? (Such a one) came and went away in regret, like a crow in a deserted house. Without the Name there is pain in the body, (crumbling) like a wall of saline earth (kallar). So long as the True One is not in the mind, the mansion (of the Lord) is not attained. Steeped in the Shabad, one finds (one's true) home, and the state beyond all desire, for ever. I ask my Guru, and having asked the Guru, I do the work. Through the Shabad let me praise (him), so that he dwells in my mind and the pain of Haumai is burnt away. In Sahaj comes the sweet union, and through Truth I am united with the True One. Those steeped in the Shabad are pure; they have cast off lust, anger and pride. They praise the Naam for ever and ever, and keep the Lord enshrined in their hearts. Why should he be forgotten from the mind, who is the support of all beings? One who dies through the Shabad stays dead (to self), and does not die a second time. Through the Shabad alone is (he) found, and love for the Lord's Name takes hold. Without the Shabad the world wanders astray, dying and being born again and again. All (the world) praises itself, (wishing its glory) to be greater than the great. Without the Guru one's own self is not recognised; what comes of mere speaking and hearing? O Nanak, when (the self) is recognised through the Shabad, no one acts in Haumai. ॥8॥
58.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If a bride is adorned without her Husband, her youth is wasted and wretched. She does not enjoy her bed in happiness; without the Husband her adornment is in vain. Great is the pain of the forsaken soul-bride; her Husband, the master of the bed, is not in her home. O mind, repeat the Lord's Name, and there will be peace. Without the Guru love is not found; joined to the Shabad, (the mind) takes on the dye (of love). Through service of the Guru peace is found; the Lord is found as Husband, and Sahaj is (her) adornment. In Truth she enjoys the bed of her Husband, with deep affection and love. Through the Guru she comes to know him and recognises him; the Guru has united her (with the Lord) of lovely virtues. O bride of the Husband, be united with the True One; the Husband has charmed (her), dyeing (her) with his love. Her mind and body have blossomed in the True One; her worth cannot be told. The happy soul-bride has the Lord as Husband in her own home; she is pure through the True Name. If the fickle mind dies within the mind, then the bride enjoys her Husband. She blends into one thread and is united, (like) a necklace of pearls about the neck. In the assembly of the Sants peace springs up; through the Guru the Naam becomes (her) support. In an instant (the mortal) springs up, in an instant wastes away; one instant he comes, the next he goes. One who recognises the Shabad and stays absorbed (in the Lord) is not tormented by death. The Master is beyond weighing and cannot be weighed; he is not attained by talk. The traders and merchants have come with their allowance written (at his door). Those who do the work of Truth receive profit by (his) will. True is the capital (of those who) meet the Guru, who has not a grain of greed. The Gurmukh will be weighed and found full weight; Truth is the scale and Truth the weight. Hope and desire, which enchant (the mind), the Guru has held back, (giving) the word of Truth. He himself has (us) weighed, and he will weigh; the weighing of the Perfect One is perfect. By talking and speaking there is no release, nor by reading loads of books. Without loving devotion to the Lord, (he) is not found by purity of the body. O Nanak, one who does not forget the Naam the Guru unites with the Creator. ॥8॥
In ਤੋੁਲਾਇਸੀ the letter ਤ carries two vowel signs (ੋ and ੁ); it is read tulaaisee, to keep the metre of the line.
59.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If the Perfect True Guru is met, the jewel of reflection (on the Lord) is found. If the mind is given to one's own Guru, love for the all-pervading (Lord) is found. The precious gift of liberation is found, which erases all failings. O brother, without the Guru there is no (true) wisdom. Ask anyone you like: Brahma, Narad, or Vyas of the Vedas. Wisdom, meditation and attunement (to the Lord) are understood (through the Guru); he leads one to speak of the Indescribable. (The Guru is) a fruitful tree, green and lush, with dense shade. Red gems, jewels and rubies: these are in the Guru's treasure-house. From the Guru's treasure-house is gained love for the pure Name. By the full grace of the Infinite One, the true merchandise is stored up. The True Guru, the giver of peace, wipes out sorrow and slays the demons. The world-ocean is treacherous and fearful; it has no shore, no far side. There is no boat, no raft, no pole and no boatman for it. The True Guru is the ship across this fearful (ocean); his glance of grace carries (us) to the far shore. If the Beloved is forgotten for even an instant, pain strikes and peace departs. Let that tongue burn, fit only for burning, which does not repeat the Naam with relish. When the body perishes there is great pain; when Jam seizes (one), one repents. Crying mine, mine, (they) have departed; body, wealth and wife went not with them. Without the Name wealth is in vain; on the road of Maya one goes astray. Let us serve the True Master; through the Guru the Indescribable is described. One comes and goes, made to wander (through births), acting as past deeds have shaped him. How can the writ of the past be erased? The writ is written by his will. Without the Lord's Name there is no release; through the Guru's teaching one is united (with him). Without him, whose are this soul and breath, I have no one. Let Haumai and possessiveness burn away; let greed and pride burn. O Nanak, let us reflect on the Shabad, (and) the treasure of virtues is found. ॥8॥
Narad is a sage of the Puranas, messenger of the gods and a devotee of Vishnu.
59.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O mind, love the Lord with such love as the lotus has for the water. Though the waves toss it about, it still blossoms in love. (The Lord) creates their life in the water; without the water they die. O mind, how will you be released without love? Within the Gurmukh (the Lord) is ever present; he bestows the treasures of devotion. O mind, love the Lord with such love as the fish has for the water. The more (water) there is, the greater its happiness, and calm (fills) its mind, body and frame. Without water it does not live for a moment; God knows the pain within (it). O mind, love the Lord with such love as the chatrik (rain-bird) has for the rain. The pools may be full and the land green, but what (is that to it), if a single drop does not fall (into its beak)? If it comes by (his) grace, that (drop) is received; (otherwise) past deeds must be borne upon head and body. O mind, love the Lord with such love as there is between water and milk. The water itself bears the boiling, and does not let the milk burn. (So the Lord) himself unites the separated, and gives them glory in Truth. O mind, love the Lord with such love as the chakvi has for the sun. She does not sleep an instant or a moment; she knows the far-off (sun) as near. The manmukh gains no understanding (of this); to the Gurmukh (the Lord) is ever near. The manmukh keeps counting up (his deeds), but what the Creator does, that alone comes to be. His worth cannot be reckoned, though everyone may long (to know it). When there is the Guru's teaching, then (he) is found; meeting the True One, there is peace. True love (for the Lord) does not break, if that True Guru is met. The precious gift of wisdom is obtained, and understanding of the three worlds. The pure Naam is not forgotten, if one becomes a buyer of virtue. The birds that pecked for food at the pool have played (their game) and gone. In a ghari or a muhat (each) must depart; the play is for today or tomorrow. Whom you unite, (O Lord), he alone is united; he goes, having won the true arena. Love does not spring up without the Guru, nor does the filth of Haumai depart. One's self is recognised as Sohang (he am I), when (the mind), pierced by the Shabad, is won over. Through the Guru one's self is recognised; what else can (one) do or have done? What is there to unite in those already united? They have met (him) through the Shabad, won over. The manmukh gains no understanding (of this); separated (from the Lord), he suffers blows. O Nanak, there is (but) one door and one home; there is no other place. ॥10॥

The chatrik (pied cuckoo) is held in Indian poetry to drink only the raindrop that falls under the Swati star, and no other water; the chakvi (ruddy shelduck) is parted from her mate at night and waits all night for the sunrise.
Sohang (Sanskrit so'ham, he am I): the recognition that one's own self is of the light of the one Lord.
60.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The manmukh (bride) strays and is led astray; strayed, she finds no place of rest. Without the Guru no one shows (the way); blinded, she comes and goes. (One who) has lost the precious gift of wisdom is cheated and robbed. O brother, Maya leads astray through doubt. The forsaken bride, strayed in doubt, does not merge in her Husband's embrace. Strayed, she roams in foreign lands; strayed, she leaves her home and goes. Strayed, she climbs mountains and high ground; her mind wavers in doubt. Separated from the very first, how can she meet (him)? Robbed by pride, she wails. The Guru will unite the separated, through the relish of the Lord and the love of the Name. In the True One and in Sahaj there is great glory, by the support of the Lord's virtues and the Name. Keep me as it pleases you, (O Lord); without you, who is my Husband? Reading letters over and over, one goes astray; the wearers of holy garb are full of pride. What can bathing at places of pilgrimage do, (when) the filth of pride is in the mind? The mind is king and sultan (over the body); without the Guru, who has ever made it understand? The precious gift of love is found, and, through the Guru, reflection on the essence. The soul-bride who has shed her self-conceit, and made the Guru's Shabad her adornment, has found that Husband, the Infinite, in her own home, through love of the Guru. By service and work for the Guru the mind becomes pure, and there is peace. (One in whose) mind the Guru's Shabad has come to dwell sheds Haumai from within. (One who) has obtained the precious gift of the Naam has profit in the mind for ever. If he comes by (his) grace, then he is found; he cannot be taken by one's own (effort). Stay attached to the Guru's feet, shedding self-conceit from within. Steeped in the True One, one gains the True One. Everyone is prone to err; only the Guru and the Creator do not err. (One whose) mind is instructed by the Guru's teaching has come to love him. O Nanak, the True One is not forgotten (by one whom) the Shabad unites with the Infinite. ॥8॥
61.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Craving for Maya the enticer: (attachment to) sons, kin, home and wife; wealth, youth, greed, avarice and pride: by these the world has been cheated. The thugs' drug of attachment has undone me; it holds sway over the whole world. O my Beloved, apart from you I have no one. Nothing but you is dear to me; when you are dear to me, there is peace. Praise the Naam with love; through the Guru's Shabad comes contentment. Whatever is seen will pass away; do not set your eyes on false attachment. (You) have come as a traveller on the road; see how the caravan moves on each day. Many speak of it in words, but without the Guru there is no understanding. If one receives the Naam and (God's) praise, one is dyed in the True One and has honour. Those who please you are good; of themselves, none is counterfeit or genuine. In the Guru's refuge one is set free; the manmukh's capital is counterfeit. The body of eight metals is the coin of the King (God); when it is minted in the Shabad, it blossoms. The Assayer himself assays it, and the (genuine) capital goes into his treasury. (O God,) your worth cannot be reckoned; I have tested it all through and through. By speaking, (your) depth is not found; one who stays steady in the True One gains honour. Through the Guru's teaching you can only be praised; beyond that, your worth cannot be told. The body in which the Naam is not dear is full of Haumai and strife. Without the Guru, divine knowledge is not gained, (and the mind keeps) the taste of Maya, of another (than God). Without virtues (this body) is of no use; the taste of Maya is insipid. In hope one is born, and in hope one eats the sweet and the bitter. Bound by hope, one is driven on, and is struck on the face again and again. Bound by faults, one is beaten; one is released through the Guru's teaching, through the Name. You alone are in every place; keep (me) as it pleases you. Through the Guru's teaching the True One dwells in the mind; the good Naam is (one's) honour and good name. (So) the disease of Haumai is cast out; through the true Shabad, utter the True One. In the skies, in the nether regions, in the three worlds, you are pervading. You yourself are devotion and love; you yourself unite (beings with you) and meet them. May Nanak never forget the Naam; as it pleases you, so is your will. ॥9॥
Thagauli: the stupefying herb (datura and the like) that thugs gave travellers in order to rob them.
Ashtadhatu: an alloy of eight metals; here the human body is the King's (God's) coin, minted in the Shabad, assayed, and taken into his treasury.
62.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). When the mind is pierced through by the Lord's Name, what else is there for me to ponder? With attention fixed on the Shabad, peace wells up; one steeped in God finds the highest peace. Keep (me) as it pleases you; the Lord's Name is my support. O mind, the Master's will is true. Attune yourself in love to him who fashioned body and mind and adorned them. If the body were cut up, a ratti (a jeweller's tiny weight) at a time, and offered into the fire, if I made body and mind the kindling of the sacrifice and burned them in the fire day after day, still none of it comes up to the Lord's Name, even if one performed lakhs and crores of such rites. If the body were sawn in two with a saw set on the head, if the body were melted away in the Himalayan snows, even then the disease would not leave the mind. None of it comes up to the Lord's Name; I have tested it all through and through. If I gave forts of gold in charity, and many fine horses and elephants, gave land, and many cows, still there would be pride and conceit within. Pierced by the Lord's Name is the mind of one to whom the Guru has given the true gift.
