Many are the notions of the stubborn mind, many the ponderings of the Vedas; many are the bonds of the soul; the door of liberation is found through the Guru. Everything falls short of Truth; above it all is a life of truth. Let everyone be called high; no one is seen to be low, for the One has fashioned all the vessels, and one light shines in the three worlds. By (his) grace alone is the True One found; the grace given from the start no one can undo. When a holy one meets the holy, contentment comes to dwell (in him) through love of the Guru. The tale of the Indescribable is pondered, if one merges in the True Guru. Drinking the nectar, he is content, and goes to the Lord's court robed in honour. In every heart the lute (of God) plays day and night; (it is heard) through the Shabad, in love. Few have come to understand this: those who, through the Guru, have taught their mind. O Nanak, (such a one) does not forget the Naam; living the Shabad, he is set free. ॥8॥
Some had their bodies sawn by the karvat (saw) at Kashi in the hope of liberation, and some ascetics went to melt their bodies in the Himalayan snows.
62.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Painted mansions are seen, with white and handsome gates; they were raised with the mind's delight, in love and attachment to another (Maya); (but) the inside is empty without love; the body collapses into a heap and (turns to) ashes. O brother, body and wealth do not stay with you (at the end). The Lord's Name is the pure wealth; the Guru gives this gift, God himself gives it. The Lord's Name is the pure wealth, (and it is had) if the Giver gives it. No account is asked hereafter of one whose friend is the Guru, the Creator. If he himself sets one free, one is freed; he himself is the Forgiver. The manmukh takes as his own the daughters and sons that destiny has brought together. (Manmukhs) delight at the sight of their wives; along with it come joy and grief. The Gurmukhs are dyed in joy through the Shabad; day and night the Lord's sweet essence is their food. The Saakat's mind wavers, for wealth must go; he is shaken again and again. Searching outside, one is ruined; the treasure is in its own place, within the home. The manmukh (bride) is robbed through her Haumai; the Gurmukh (bride) gathers it into her lap. O Saakat without virtue, recognise where you came from. This body is made of blood and seed; know that it is bound for the fire. This frail body is in the power of the breath; on the forehead is the true, unfailing mark (of his command). A long life is what one asks for; no one wishes to die. (But) a life of peace is said to be his in whom, through the Guru, that Lord dwells. Of what account do I hold one without the Name, who has no sight of the Lord, of the Guru? As one is deluded by a dream at night, as long as sleep lasts, so the poor soul is in the power of the she-serpent (Maya), with Haumai and duality within. When the Guru's teaching is received, one comes to see that this world, this whole realm, is a dream. As fire dies when water is poured on it, as a child (is satisfied) by its mother's milk, as the lotus cannot live without water, and the fish dies without water, (so,) O Nanak, the Gurmukh (lives) joined to the Lord's sweet essence; I live by singing the Lord's virtues. ॥8॥
63.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Seeing the frightening mountain, (the soul-bride) was afraid in her parents' home. High and arduous is the mountain, and she has no ladder to climb it. Through the Guru she came to know (the Lord) within; joined (to him) by the Guru, she crossed over. O brother, the world-ocean is hard to cross and terrifying. One whom the perfect True Guru meets in love, the Guru carries across by the Lord's Name. If I keep in mind that I must go, and know (the world) is passing away, that whoever has come shall depart, and only the Guru, the Creator, is undying, then the True One is to be praised, with love, in the true place (the Sat Sangat). Beautiful gates, houses and mansions, thousands of strong forts, elephants, saddled horses, armies by the lakh beyond count: none of it went along with anyone; the senseless wore themselves out and died. Gold and silver are amassed, (but) wealth is a net, an entanglement. One may have one's proclamation cried throughout the world, (yet) without the Name, death hangs over one's head. When the body falls and the soul's play is over, what will be the plight of the evildoers? One delights at the sight of one's sons, and of the wife on her husband's bed; perfume and sandalwood are applied, (and one delights in) clothes, beauty and adornment; (but in the end) dust is mixed with dust, and one departs, leaving house and home. One has oneself called chief or king, raja, rao or khan; one is styled chaudhari or rao, and burns up in pride. (But) the manmukh has forgotten the Naam, and is like a reed scorched in a forest fire. Whoever has come into the world will depart, acting in Haumai all along. The whole world is a chamber of soot; body, mind and frame (are soiled) in its ash. Those the Guru has kept are spotless; through the Shabad he has put out (their) fire. O Nanak, one crosses over through the True Name of him who is King above all kings. May I never forget the Lord's Name; the jewel of the Lord's Name is (my) capital. The manmukhs wasted away and died in the terrifying world-ocean; the Gurmukhs crossed the fathomless (ocean). ॥8॥
64.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One may sit at home, taking it for a lasting abode, (yet) there is ever the worry of departing. It could be known as a lasting abode only if the world stayed unmoving. How can the world be a lasting abode? With faith, tie up good deeds as provisions (for the journey), and stay joined to the Name. The yogi sits fixed in his posture; the mulla sits in his mukaam (his seat). Pandits expound their books; Siddhas sit in the temple of a god. Gods, Siddhas, ganas (Shiva's attendants), gandharvas (heavenly singers), silent sages, sheikhs, pirs and commanders: march upon march they have gone away, and the rest too are bound to go. Sultans, khans, kings and nobles have broken camp and gone, one after another. In a ghari or a muhat one must go; understand, O heart: you too are about to arrive (there). In words it is told, but rare is one who understands. Nanak humbly prays: he (alone) is in the water, on the land, and in the sky. Allah, the Unseen, the Inaccessible, the Almighty, the Creator, the Bountiful: the whole world comes and goes; the Merciful One alone is lasting. He alone may be called lasting, on whose head no writ is written. Sky and earth shall pass away; he, the One, alone is lasting. By day the sun passes on, by night the moon passes on; the stars in lakhs fade away. He, the One, alone is lasting; O Nanak, speak this truth. The seventeen Ashtapadis of the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Mukaam (Persian maqam): a halt or lasting abode; a mulla's or fakir's mukaam is his seat (takia).
64.2: Sri Raag, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. When, through the Guru, (God) shows his grace, devotion is performed; without the Guru there is no devotion. When one merges one's self in (the Guru's) self and understands, then one becomes pure. The dear Lord is true, true is (his) Bani; through the Shabad comes union (with him). O brother, why has one empty of devotion come into the world? He did not serve the perfect Guru, and he has wasted his life in vain. The Lord is himself the Life of the world and the Giver; he himself forgives (beings) and joins them to himself. What are these helpless beings and creatures? What can anyone say or tell? Through the Guru he himself gives glory; he himself has (them) serve him. Seeing his family, (a man) is lured into attachment; (yet) when he departs, (none of it) goes with him. Serving the True Guru, one has found the treasure of virtues, whose worth cannot be reckoned. God, my dear Lord, is the (true) friend; in the end he becomes the companion. In this world, the parents' home, is the Life of the world, the Giver; (forgetting him) the manmukh has lost (his) honour. Without the True Guru none knows the path; the blind one has nowhere to rest. The Lord, the giver of peace, did not dwell in (his) mind; in the end he departed repenting. In this world, the parents' home, (those who) through the Guru's teaching have enshrined in the mind the Life of the world, the Giver, worship him every moment, day and night, and have cast off Haumai and attachment. One becomes like the one in whose love one is dyed; (so such a one) merges in the True One alone. He himself casts his glance of grace and instils love; (then one) reflects through the Guru's Shabad. When the True Guru is served, Sahaj wells up, once Haumai and craving are killed. The Lord, the Giver of virtues, dwells ever in (his) mind; (he) has kept the True One enshrined in the heart. My God is pure for ever; he is found through a pure mind. (When) the treasure of the Lord's Name dwells in the mind, all the pain of Haumai departs. The True Guru has proclaimed the Shabad; I am ever a sacrifice (to him). (One) may say in one's own mind and heart (that self-conceit is gone), and have (others) say it too, but without the Guru self-conceit does not go. The dear Lord loves devotion and gives peace; by his grace he enshrines himself in the mind. O Nanak, God himself gives honour and awareness, and through the Guru he himself gives glory. ॥8॥
65.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who do their deeds in Haumai are struck by the rod of Jam, which comes upon them. Those who serve the True Guru are saved, their attention lovingly fixed on the Lord. O mind, meditate on the Naam through the Guru. Those for whom the Creator wrote it from the beginning, (by deeds done) before, merge in the Naam through the Guru's teaching. Without the True Guru faith does not arise, and no love for the Naam takes hold. (Such a one) finds no peace even in dreams; he sleeps sunk in sorrow. Even if one longs greatly that (such a one) should repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the imprint of (his) past deeds cannot be erased. The devotees have accepted the Lord's will; those devotees are accepted at (his) door. With love the Guru makes the Shabad firm (in the heart), but without (God's) grace it cannot be received. (The manmukh is like a poisonous plant:) even if it is watered with nectar a hundred times, poisonous fruit still springs up on it quickly. Those people are true and pure whose love is for the True Guru. They live by the True Guru's will, having cast off the poison of Haumai, its vice. By the mind's stubbornness one is not set free by any means; go and search the Simritis and the Shastras. Joining the company of the holy (Guru) and living by the Guru's Shabad, they are saved. The Lord's Name is a treasure that has no end, no near shore and no far shore. Through the Guru, they alone are made beautiful on whom the Creator shows his grace. O Nanak, the Giver is One; there is no other at all. He is found by the Guru's grace; he is attained through (his) mercy. ॥8॥
66.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The bird on the tree (of the body) is lovely when it pecks at the True (Name) in the Guru's love. It drinks the Lord's nectar and abides in Sahaj; it does not fly about, nor does it come and go. It has found its dwelling in its own true home, merged in the Name of the Lord, Har Har. O mind, do the work the Guru gives. If you walk in the Guru's will, you will stay absorbed in the Lord's Name day and night. The birds on the trees look lovely, (but) they fly off and go in all four directions. The farther they fly, the greater their pain; ever they burn and wail. Without the Guru the mansion (of the Lord) is not seen, nor do they obtain the nectar fruits. The Gurmukh is (the very form of) Brahm, a tree ever green, abiding in the True One, in Sahaj and in love. He has cut away the three branches (the three qualities of Maya), fixing his attention on the one Shabad. The nectar fruit is (the Name of) the one Lord alone; he himself gives it to eat. The manmukhs have withered where they stand; they bear neither fruit nor shade. One should not sit near them; they have neither home nor village. They are cut down and burnt day after day; they have neither the Shabad nor the Name. By (his) Hukam beings do their deeds, and by the stored imprint of deeds done they wander (in the round of births). By Hukam (the Lord) is beheld; wherever you send, there one must go. By Hukam the Lord, Har Har, dwells in the mind; by Hukam one merges in the True One. The wretched fools do not know the Hukam; they wander about, gone astray. They do their deeds by the stubbornness of the mind, and are ruined day after day. Peace does not come within them, nor does love for the True One take hold. The Gurmukhs' faces are beautiful, (for they abide) in love and affection for the Guru. Through true devotion they are steeped in the True One; at the True One's door they are found true. Their coming (into the world) is approved; they bring deliverance to all their line. All do their deeds under (the Lord's) gaze; no one is outside (his) gaze. As the True One looks upon someone, such does that one become. O Nanak, all glory lies in the Name; (the Name) is attained through (his) mercy. ॥8॥
In this shabad the bird is the soul and the tree the body; the true feed it pecks is the Lord's Name.
66.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through the Guru the Naam is meditated on; the manmukh gains no understanding (of it). Through the Guru faces are ever radiant, (for) the Lord has come to dwell in the mind. In Sahaj alone is peace found, and in Sahaj one remains absorbed. O brother, become the servant of (the Lord's) servants. This is the Guru's service, this the devotion the Guru teaches; rare is the one who attains it. The soul-brides keep their wedded bliss for ever, if they walk in the True Guru's love. (They) find the Husband, ever unshaken, who neither dies nor goes away. She who is united through the Shabad is never parted; she rests merged in her Husband's embrace. The Lord is pure, exceedingly bright; without the Guru he cannot be found. One who only reads texts does not understand (this); the wearers of religious garb stray, lost in doubt. Through the Guru's teaching the Lord is found for ever, and the Lord's sweet taste stays on the tongue. (The one who) has ended attachment to Maya through the Guru's teaching (abides) in Sahaj and in love. Without the Shabad the world wanders in misery; (Maya) has devoured the manmukhs. Through the Shabad alone is the Naam meditated on; through the Shabad alone one merges in the True One. Led astray by Maya, the Siddhas wander; their Samadhi does not settle in (the Lord's) love. (Maya) pervades all three worlds, and clings (to all) exceedingly. Without the Guru liberation is not attained, nor does the double-mindedness (born) of Maya go. What is it that is called Maya? What deeds does Maya do? (Under Maya) this soul is bound in pain and pleasure, and does its deeds in Haumai. Without the Shabad doubt does not end, nor does Haumai leave from within. Without love there is no devotion; without the Shabad one is not accepted (at the Lord's door). Through the Shabad Haumai is slain, and the wandering that Maya brings is gone. Through the Guru the treasure of the Naam is obtained, in Sahaj and in love. Without the Guru virtues are not discerned, and without virtues there is no devotion. (In whose) mind the Lord, lover of devotion, has come to dwell, (that one) has met that God in Sahaj. O Nanak, let us praise the Lord through the Shabad; (this gift) is attained through (his) mercy. ॥8॥
67.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). My God himself made attachment to Maya; he himself leads (beings) astray in doubt. The manmukhs do their deeds but do not understand; (such a one) wastes his life in vain. Gurbani is the light in this world; by (his) grace it comes to dwell in the mind. O mind, repeat the Naam, and there is peace. Let us praise the Perfect Guru, and in Sahaj that God is met. With the mind fixed on the Lord's feet, doubt has gone and fear has fled. Let us live the Shabad through the Guru, and the Lord comes to dwell in the mind. (Then) one merges in the True One, in the home within, in (his) mansion, and Jamkaal cannot devour (one). Nama the calico printer and Kabir the weaver attained the highest state through the Perfect Guru. Knowers of God, they recognised the Shabad and cast off Haumai and (the sense of) caste. Gods and men sing their Bani; no one can blot (their glory) out, O brother. The demon's son (Prahlad) read nothing of rites, religious duties or disciplines; he knew no love of another. Meeting the True Guru, he became pure, and he utters the Naam day and night. He reads of the One alone and understands the one Name alone; he knows no other. The six orders of garb, the yogis and the sannyasis, are led astray by doubt when they lack the Guru. Should they serve the True Guru, they find the high state and the (right) way of living, enshrining the Dear Lord in the mind. (The one whose) mind is joined to the True Bani brings his coming and going to an end. The pandits read and read and expound their disputes; without the Guru they stray in doubt. The round of the eighty-four lakh (births) befalls them; without the Shabad one finds no liberation. When one remembers the Name, then one attains the high state, when the True Guru brings (one) into union (with the Lord). In the Sat Sangat the Lord's Name springs up (in the heart), when the True Guru is met in love. Let me offer my mind and body, cast off my self, and walk in the True Guru's love. I am ever a sacrifice to my Guru, who joins (my) mind to the Lord. That one is a Brahmin who knows Brahm and is dyed in love with the Lord. God dwells near, within every heart; (yet) a rare one has known (this), through the Guru. O Nanak, the one who has recognised (the Lord) through the Guru's Shabad receives the Naam, and glory. ॥8॥
Namdev was a chhimba, a calico printer, and Kabir a weaver; both were Bhagats of castes counted low, and the hymns of both are in the Guru Granth Sahib.
The demon's son is Prahlad, son of the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu), who held to devotion to God through all his father's torments.

The six orders (khat darshan): the six sects of ascetics known by their garb, such as the yogis, jangams, sannyasis, bairagis, sarevras (Jains) and Buddhists; some read it as the six schools of Hindu philosophy.
68.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). All the world longs for Sahaj, but without the Guru it cannot be attained. Pandits and astrologers have grown weary of reading and reading; the wearers of religious garb stray, lost in doubt. Meeting the Guru, Sahaj is attained, when (God) shows his grace by his own will. O brother, without the Guru there is no Sahaj. From the Shabad alone Sahaj wells up, and that True Lord is found. Praise sung in Sahaj is accepted; without Sahaj all talk (of faith) is in vain. In Sahaj alone devotion wells up; in Sahaj (one abides) in (the Lord's) love and in detachment. From Sahaj alone come peace and calm; without Sahaj, life is in vain. In Sahaj praise (the Lord) for ever and ever; in Sahaj enter Samadhi. (The one who) in Sahaj alone utters (the Lord's) virtues and worships with loving attention: through the Shabad alone the Lord dwells in (that) mind, and (that) tongue savours the Lord's sweet taste. (Those who,) entering the True One's refuge, have in Sahaj destroyed death: in Sahaj the Lord's Name has come to dwell in (their) minds, as they do the true work. Greatly fortunate are those who have found (the Name); they remain absorbed in Sahaj. Within Maya, Sahaj does not well up; Maya (draws one) into the love of another. Doing the deeds of the manmukh, one burns in Haumai and burns (oneself) away. (His) birth and death do not end; again and again he comes and goes. In the three qualities Sahaj is not found; the three qualities lead one astray in doubt. What use is reading, reflecting and expounding, when one goes astray from the very root? Sahaj is in the fourth state; through the Guru it falls into one's lap. The Name of (the Lord) beyond the three qualities is the treasure; in Sahaj alone does (its) understanding come. The virtuous have praised (the Lord); (merged) in the True One, true is their renown. (The Lord) will unite (even) those who have strayed, in Sahaj; through the Shabad union (with him) comes about. Without Sahaj all (the world) is blind; attachment to Maya is pitch darkness. In Sahaj alone has understanding come, through the true and infinite Shabad. Through the Perfect Guru the Creator himself has forgiven (them) and united (them with himself). In Sahaj the Unseen is recognised: the Fearless, the Light, the Formless. (He is) the one Giver of all beings, who merges (each) light in (his) Light. Let us praise him through the perfect Shabad, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore. The wealth of the wise is the Naam; in Sahaj they trade (in it). Day and night they reap the profit of the Lord's Name; (their) storehouses are full and never run out. O Nanak, no shortage ever comes, (for) the Great Giver has given (them). ॥10॥
69.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). On meeting the True Guru one does not fall into the round (of births) again, and the pain of birth and death is gone. Through the perfect Shabad all understanding comes, and one remains absorbed in the Lord's Name. O my mind, fix your attention on the True Guru. (Then) the pure Naam, ever fresh, comes of its own accord to dwell in the mind. Dear Lord, keep (me) in your refuge; as you keep (me), so must I live. (The one who) dies while living, through the Guru's Shabad, crosses the world-ocean through the Guru. The Name is obtained by great good fortune; through the Guru's teaching, through the Shabad, (life) is made beautiful. God the Creator himself comes to dwell in the mind, and one remains absorbed in Sahaj. To some, being manmukh, the Shabad is not pleasing; (such a one) is bound in bondage and made to wander. Through the eighty-four lakh (births) he comes again and again; he has wasted his life in vain. Bliss dwells in the devotees' minds; through the True Shabad they are dyed in (the Lord's) love. Day and night they sing (his) virtues; ever pure, they stay absorbed in the Name, in Sahaj. Through the Guru they speak the nectar Bani, recognising in all the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram). They serve the One alone and worship the One alone; through the Guru (they tell) the story of the Indescribable. Let us serve the True Master; through the Guru he comes to dwell in the mind. Ever dyed in love with the True One are those whom he, in his grace, unites (with himself). (The Lord) himself does and himself causes all to be done; some who are asleep he wakes. O Nanak, (the Lord) himself unites (them) with himself, absorbing (them) in the Shabad. ॥8॥
69.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). When the True Guru is served, the mind becomes pure and the body is made holy. Bliss (wells up) in the mind, lasting peace is found, and the deep, unfathomable (Lord) is met. Sitting in the true Sangat, the mind grows steady in the True One, in (his) Name. O mind, serve the True Guru with nothing held back. By serving the True Guru the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, and not a speck of filth clings (to it). Through the true Shabad honour springs up, and (one gains) the True Name of the True One. Those who have killed Haumai and recognised (him): I am a sacrifice to them. The manmukhs do not know the True One; they have no shelter and no place anywhere. Truth (the Name) is their food and Truth their clothing, and in the True One alone is their dwelling. They ever praise the True One, and their abode is in the true Shabad. They have recognised the all-pervading Lord everywhere, and through the Guru's teaching they dwell in their own home within. The True One is what they see and Truth is what they speak; their body and mind become true. Their teaching is true and their counsel is of Truth; the glory of those made true is lasting. Those who have forgotten the True One have departed in misery, weeping. Those who have not served the True Guru: to what end did they come into the world? Bound at Jam's door they are beaten, and no one hears their cries and pleas. They have wasted their life in vain; again and again they die and are born. Those who saw this world on fire and ran for refuge to the True Guru: in them the True Guru has firmly set the True One (the Name), and (taught them) to live always in Truth and in restraint. The True Guru is the true ship; through the Shabad the world-ocean is crossed. (Beings) kept wandering through the eighty-four lakh forms of life; without the True Guru there was no liberation. The pandits and the silent sages have worn themselves out with reading and reading; in the love of another they have lost their honour. The True Guru has made the Shabad heard: apart from the True One there is no other. Those whom the True One has joined (to himself) hold fast to the True One, and day after day they do the true work. They have found a dwelling in their own home within; they live in the mansion of the True One. O Nanak, the devotees are ever at peace; they stay absorbed in the True Name. ॥8॥
70.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When someone is beset by great hardship, and no one will give him shelter, when enemies turn on him to do him harm, and even his kin run off and stand apart, when every prop gives way and all his support is gone, (even then,) if the Supreme Lord comes into his mind, not even a hot wind touches him. The Master is the strength of the powerless. He neither comes nor goes (is neither born nor dies); he stands for ever. Through the Guru's Shabad, come to know him, the True One. If someone grows weak, suffering the pain of nakedness and hunger, with not a penny to his name and no one to give him comfort, if no one meets his need or his aim, and no work of his comes to anything, (even then,) if the Supreme Lord comes into his mind, his rule becomes unshakeable. One who is weighed down by worry upon worry, whose body is seized by disease, who is wrapped up in household and family, now in joy and now in grief, who roams the four directions and never sits still for a moment, (even then,) if the Supreme Lord comes into his mind, his body and mind grow cool and calm. One whom lust, anger and attachment hold in their sway, a miser whose love is set on greed, who has committed the four great sins and (other) wrongs, and has become a demon who slays, who has never let any sacred book, hymn or poem reach his ears, (even then,) if the Supreme Lord comes into his mind, he is carried across by remembering him for an instant. One may know the Shastras, the Simritis and the four Vedas by heart and reflect on them; be an ascetic, a master of austerities, a yogi, and journey to the places of pilgrimage; perform twice the six rites, and offer worship after bathing; (but) if love for the Supreme Lord has not taken hold, he surely goes to hell. One may have kingdoms, estates and lordships, and pleasures to enjoy in plenty, lovely, beautiful gardens; the puffed-up man's command may hold sway; he may be eagerly caught up in shows and amusements of many kinds; (but) if the Supreme Lord has not come into his mind, he has passed into the life-form of a snake. One may be very rich, of good conduct, honoured, with a spotless way of life; he may be bound in love to mother, father, sons, brothers and friends; armies of quiver-girt warriors may salute him, and all may answer him with ji, ji; (but) if the Supreme Lord has not come into his mind, he is dragged off and cast into Rasatal (the lowest hell). One may have no disease in the body and no flaw at all, no anxiety or sorrow of any kind; death may never cross his mind, and day and night he may revel in pleasures; he may have made everything his own, with no misgiving in his heart; (but) if the Supreme Lord has not come into his mind, he falls into the power of Jam's servants. The one on whom the Supreme Lord shows mercy finds the company of the holy. The more one keeps that company, the more love for the Lord (grows). He himself is the Master of both ends, here and hereafter; there is no other place (of refuge). O Nanak, it is when the True Guru is pleased that the True Name is found. ॥9॥
The four great sins: the gravest sins of the Hindu law books; by one common count, killing a Brahmin, drinking liquor, stealing gold and adultery with the teacher's wife.
The six rites (khat karam): the six duties of a Brahmin: studying and teaching the Vedas, performing and officiating at sacrifice, giving and receiving gifts.
71.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I do not know what it is that pleases (God). O mind, search out the path. The meditators sit absorbed in meditation; the learned put their knowledge into practice; (yet) only a rare one has known God. The Bhagauti (devotee of Vishnu) lives by his rules and observances; the yogi says (he is) liberated; the ascetic is absorbed in austerities. The silent sage keeps his vow of silence; (one is) a sannyasi, (another) a celibate; the Udasi is absorbed in his detachment. (Some practise) devotion of the nine kinds; the pandit calls out the Vedas; the householder is absorbed in the duties of the household. Some call out a single word (Alakh), some take on many guises, some are naked avadhuts; some wear a special robe, some stage shows, some keep vigil through the night; some bathe at places of pilgrimage. Some fast and go without food, some will touch no one; some stay hidden away and let no one see them; some are wise only in their own minds. Not one of them has called himself lacking; all say they have found (God). (But) the devotee is the one whom (God) unites (with himself). All clever reasoning and every device I have renounced, and I have entered (God's) refuge; Nanak has fallen at the Guru's feet. ॥8॥

The nine kinds of devotion (navadha bhakti), as the Vaishnavas count them: hearing of God, singing his praise, remembering him, serving his feet, worship, bowing down, servitude, friendship and offering up the self.
71.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Sri Raag, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O Lord), within the yogis you are the yogi; within those who enjoy (the world) you are the enjoyer. No one has found your limit, in heaven, on this earth or in the underworld. I am a sacrifice, I am devoted, I am offered up to your Name. You created the world, and set each and every one to their tasks. Having made creation and cast the dice (in the world's game of chaupar), you watch over what you have made. (The Lord) is seen plainly in the visible expanse (of creation); everyone yearns for the Name. (Yet) without the True Guru no one has found (him); all are held spellbound in the net of Maya. Let us be a sacrifice to the True Guru, meeting whom the supreme state is attained. What gods, men and silent sages long for, the True Guru has made known. How is the Sat Sangat to be known? (It is the place) where the one Naam alone is spoken. (Repeating) the one Naam is (God's) Hukam; O Nanak, the True Guru has made (this) known. This world has been led astray in doubt; you yourself, (O Lord), have made it stray from you. Anguish has seized the forsaken soul-brides, who have no good fortune. What are the marks of the forsaken soul-brides? Strayed from their Husband, they wander about without honour. Soiled are the clothes of those women, and their night (of life) passes in pain. What deed did the happy soul-brides do? (They) have received the fruit written from before. With a glance of his grace, (the Lord) himself unites (them with himself). Those whom (the Lord) has led to accept his Hukam: within them (he) has made the Shabad dwell. Those companions are the happy soul-brides who love their Husband Lord. Those who have come to relish (God's) will: from within them (he) has taken doubt away. O Nanak, the True Guru is to be known as the one who unites all (with the Lord). Through meeting the True Guru, the fruit has been obtained by the one who has cast out self-conceit from within. The suffering of a corrupt intellect is cut away, and good fortune has come to settle on (that one's) forehead. (O Lord), your Word is Amrit; it is absorbed into the hearts of your devotees. When the service that brings peace is kept within, you cast your glance of grace and carry (them) across. The True Guru should be known to have been met when, meeting him, one comes to utter the Naam. Without the True Guru no one has found (him); all have worn themselves out performing rites. I am a sacrifice to the True Guru, who has set on the path the one who was lost in doubt. If (the Guru) casts his glance of grace, he himself blends (one into the Lord). (O Lord), you pervade all; (yet) that Creator has hidden himself. O Nanak, through the Guru he has become manifest in the one within whom the Creator has placed (his) light. The Master himself has honoured (his servant); giving soul and body, he fashioned (him). He has kept the honour of his servant, placing both hands on (his) forehead. All disciplines and clever ways have fallen short; my God knows everything. He has made (his servant's) glory shine openly, and all the world hails (him). (God) did not weigh my merits and faults; God has kept to his own age-old way (of grace). Hugging (me) to his bosom, he has kept (me) safe; not even a hot wind touches (me). I have meditated on God with mind and body, (and) have obtained the fruit my heart longed for. You are the Master over the heads of kings and emperors; Nanak lives by repeating (your) Name. You yourself brought yourself forth (as the world), and made and displayed this play that seems other (than you). Everywhere the True One alone is at work; to whom he pleases he gives (this) understanding. (The one who) has grasped (this) by the Guru's grace: there, (in that heart, the Lord) has done away with attachment to Maya. Showing his grace, (the Lord) himself absorbs (that one into himself). (O Lord), you are the gopi, the river (Yamuna) and the cowherd; you yourself have raised up the earth. By your Hukam you have fashioned the vessels (of the body); you yourself break them and make them anew. Those who have joined their mind to the True Guru have put an end to the love of another. Pure is the light of those beings; they leave (this world) having made their life fair. (O Lord), your goodness endures for ever and ever; night and day I sing (your) praises. (You) give your gifts unasked. Says Nanak, keep the True One in your heart. ॥24॥
Each stanza of this hymn closes with ਜੀਉ (jeeo), a word of loving address that rounds off the line; it adds nothing to the sense.

The gopi (milkmaid), the river (Yamuna) and the cowherd recall the story of Krishna in Braj: all of them are God himself. ਗੋਇ is the earth; some read it as the hill Govardhan, which Krishna is said to have lifted.
73.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Falling at (his) feet, I seek to please him (the Lord). The True Guru, the Purakh, has united (me with him); none is as great as he. The Lord of the world, my own, is most dear; he is sweeter than mother and father. Sisters, brothers, all friends: (O Lord,) there is no one like you. By your Hukam alone the month of Saavan (the rains) has come; I have yoked the plough of Sat (truthful living). I have begun to sow the Naam, hoping that the Lord will gather a heap of grain, the harvest of his grace. Having met the Guru, I recognise the One alone; I do not know how to write any second paper (account). The Lord has set (me) to a single task; (O Lord,) as it pleases you, so see it through. O brothers, you too enjoy (this Naam) and feast on it. In the (Lord's) court, the Guru has clothed (me) in a robe of honour. I have become the headman of the village (of the body); the five rivals I have bound and brought in. (O Lord,) I have come to your refuge; the five farmers have become my tenants. No one can lift his head (against me); O Nanak, the village (of the body) is thickly settled. I am a sacrifice, I am devoted (to you); O King, I meditate on you alone. You have peopled (my) desolate ruin-mound; I am a sacrifice to you. I meditate on the beloved Lord every day, and obtain the fruit I wish for in my mind. He has set all (my) affairs right, and taken away the hunger of the mind. I have given up all (worldly) busyness; I serve the Lord of the world, the True One. The Lord's treasure of the Naam is the nine treasures; I have tied it tight in the hem of my cloth. I have found the joy of all joys; the Guru has made the Shabad dwell within (me). Placing his hand on (my) forehead, the True Guru, the Purakh, has shown (me the Lord). I have built a dharamsal (a house of worship) of the True One; I seek out the Guru's Sikhs and meet them. I wash (their) feet and wave the fan, and bowing low again and again, I fall at the feet of each. Hearing of these things, (I) came to the Guru; (he) made firm in (me) the Naam, giving and cleansing. The whole poor world is set free, O Nanak, once (the Guru) puts it aboard the true boat. All creation serves (you) day and night; (O Lord,) give ear and hear (my) prayer. I have tested all (creation) through and through; (those who are freed,) he himself, being pleased, has set free. Now the command of the Merciful One has gone out; no one falls upon another to cause him pain. All dwell in comfort; this has become a reign of humility. Softly, drop by drop, the nectar rains down; what I speak, the Master makes me speak. Great is the pride I have placed in you; you yourself will accept (me). (O Lord,) your devotees ever hunger for you; O Lord, fulfil my longings. O giver of peace, grant (me) the sight of you, and take me into your embrace. I have found no other as great as you. You are in the continents, the worlds and the underworlds; you pervade every place and the spaces between; O Nanak, the True One is the devotees' support. I am a humble little wrestler of the Lord of the world; meeting the Guru, I have (tied) a high-crested dumala (turban). The whole chhinjh (wrestling fair) has gathered, and the Beloved Lord himself sits watching. Pipes, drums and kettledrums are sounding; the wrestlers have come down (into the ring) and are taking their rounds. I have pinned down the five young (wrestlers); the Guru has given (me) a pat on the back. All have come here together (into the arena of the world), (but) they will go home by separate roads. The Gurmukhs have gone with their profit; the manmukhs have left, losing even the capital. (O Lord,) you are beyond colour and mark, (yet,) O Lord, you are seen present and manifest. Your devotees hear (of you) over and over and meditate on you; they are imbued with (the love of you,) the treasure of virtues. Age after age, I do the loving service of the Beloved (Lord); the Guru has cut my rope (of bondage). I shall not dance in the arena again; Nanak, seeking, has found the chance. ॥21॥
The five rivals and the five young wrestlers are lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride; the five farmers who become tenants are the five senses, now under control.
A chhinjh is a village wrestling fair; the winning wrestler ties a turban with a high crest (dumala), and a pat on the back (thapi) is the mark of praise.
74.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Sri Raag, Ghar 1, Pahare, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O merchant friend, in the first watch of the night (of life), by (the Lord's) Hukam (the soul) was placed in the womb. Upside down within, he practises austerity, O merchant friend, and prays to the Master. He utters his prayers to the Master; upside down, absorbed in meditation, he stays lovingly attuned. Naked he came into the world, and naked he will go again. As the pen has run upon his forehead, such (is the stock) the soul carries with it. Says Nanak, in the first watch the mortal was placed in the womb by (the Lord's) Hukam. O merchant friend, in the second watch of the night, the meditation (on the Lord) has been forgotten. The child is dandled from hand to hand, O merchant friend, as Kanh (Krishna) was in the house of Jasuda (Yashoda). The mortal is dandled from hand to hand, and the mother says: this is my son. O heedless, foolish mind of mine, remember (him): at the end nothing is yours. He does not know the one who fashioned and made him; (O mind,) hold that knowledge within. Says Nanak, in the second watch the mortal has forgotten the meditation (on the Lord). O merchant friend, in the third watch of the night, the mind is set on wealth and youth. You do not remember the Lord's Name, O merchant friend, through which you, who are bound, would go free. The mortal does not remember the Lord's Name; in the company of Maya he has lost his senses. Dyed in wealth and drunk with youth, he has wasted this precious life. He did not trade in dharma, nor make good deeds his friend. Says Nanak, in the third watch the mortal's mind is set on wealth and youth. O merchant friend, in the fourth watch of the night, the reaper has come to the field. When Jam seized him and led him away, O merchant friend, no one learnt the secret. No one found the secret or the purpose of the Lord, when Jam seized him and led him away. False weeping rose all around him; in an instant he became a stranger. He received that very thing on which he had set his love. Says Nanak, O mortal, in the fourth watch the reaper has cut the field. ॥4॥

Pahare (the watches): the four watches of the night are the stages of a life. The mortal is a travelling merchant, come from the Lord's door to trade in the Name in this world, who spends one night here.
Kanh (Krishna) was raised as a child by Jasuda (Yashoda), wife of the cowherd Nand of Gokul, and was fondly passed from hand to hand.
75.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O merchant friend, in the first watch of the night, (the mortal) has a child's understanding and is heedless. He drinks milk and is played with, O merchant friend; mother and father love their son. Great is the parents' fondness for the son; attachment to Maya (holds) all the world. By the union (of past deeds) he came, as his deeds had earned; his own conduct has made him do (his) work. Without the Lord's Name there is no liberation; (the world) is drowned in the love of duality. Says Nanak, O mortal, remembering the Lord in the first watch, you will be set free. O merchant friend, in the second watch of the night, (his) mind is drunk on the wine of brimming youth. Day and night he is gripped by lust, O merchant friend; the Naam is not in the blind one's mind. The Lord's Name is not within his heart; he knows other relishes, the sharp and the sweet. (In him) there is no wisdom, no meditation, no virtue, no restraint; O false ones, you will be born and die. There is no pilgrimage, no fasting, no purity, no restraint; no rite, no duty, no worship. O Nanak, deliverance comes through love and devotion; in double-mindedness, the other (the love of Maya) takes hold. O merchant friend, in the third watch of the night, swans (white hairs) have come down upon the lake (of the head). Youth ebbs and old age is winning, O merchant friend; as each day goes, the span of life shrinks. O blind one, at the last moment you will repent, when Jam seizes you and leads you away. All that you kept, calling it your own, in an instant became another's. Understanding is gone, shrewdness has fled; having done wrong, he repents. Says Nanak, O mortal, in the third watch remember God, lovingly attuned. O merchant friend, in the fourth watch of the night, he has grown old and the body is worn thin. Darkness lies on his eyes and he cannot see, O merchant friend; with his ears he does not hear words. Blind in the eyes, with no taste on the tongue, his vigour and strength are spent. There is no virtue within; how can he find peace? The manmukh keeps coming and going. The ripened stalk snaps, breaks and perishes; one comes and departs: what is there to be proud of? Says Nanak, O mortal, in the fourth watch recognise the Shabad through the Guru. The end of those (numbered) breaths has come, O merchant friend; old age, the tyrant, sits upon the shoulders. (In whom) not a particle of virtue has settled, O merchant friend, (his) faults will bind him and carry him off. One who goes (from here) with the discipline of virtue suffers no blow, and for him there is no birth or death. Death's net and Jam cannot even eye him; through loving devotion he crosses (the ocean of) fear. He departs with honour, merges in Sahaj, and does away with every pain. Says Nanak, the mortal is freed through the Guru, and receives honour from the True One. ॥5॥
76.1: Sri Raag, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O merchant friend, in the first watch of the night, the Lord placed (the soul) in the womb. (There) he meditates on the Lord and utters the Lord, O merchant friend, cherishing the Name of the Lord, Har Har. He repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and worships; within the fire (of the womb) he lives by repeating the Lord. He is born outside (the womb) and comes before (his parents') eyes; father and mother are delighted. O mortal, remember the one whose gift this (child) is; reflect on him in your heart through the Guru. Says Nanak, O mortal, in the first watch the Lord is meditated on when he shows his grace. O merchant friend, in the second watch of the night, the mind has turned to the love of another. He is reared with (cries of) mine, mine, O merchant friend; mother and father take him and hold him close. Mother and father ever hold him to their breast, thinking in their minds that he will earn and feed (them). The fool does not recognise the Giver; he clings to what is given. One who becomes Gurmukh reflects (on this), and meditates on the Lord, his mind lovingly attuned. Says Nanak, O mortal, in the second watch death never devours him. O merchant friend, in the third watch of the night, the mind is caught up in the house and the snares (of the world). He thinks of wealth and hoards wealth, O merchant friend, but does not cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har. He never cherishes the Name of the Lord, Har Har, which stands by one at the last. False are this wealth, these possessions and Maya; at the last he abandons them and goes, regretting. One on whom (the Lord) shows grace and whom he brings to the Guru cherishes the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Says Nanak, O mortal, in the third watch such ones go and meet with the Lord. O merchant friend, in the fourth watch of the night, the Lord has brought on the time to depart. Serve the True Guru, knowing him to be perfect, O merchant friend; the whole night is passing away. Serve the Lord every moment and make no delay at all, so that you become steadfast through the ages. Enjoy delight with the Lord for ever, and be rid of the pains of birth and death. Know the Guru, the True Guru, to be no different from the Master; meeting (the Guru), devotion to the Lord grows sweet. Says Nanak, O mortal, in the fourth watch the devotees' night bears fruit. ॥4॥
77.1: Sri Raag, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O merchant friend, in the first watch of the night, (the Lord) gives (the soul) a place in the womb. In ten months (he) has made a human being, O merchant friend; (he) grants a span of time, (in which beings) do their deeds. (He) has given the span for deeds to be done, according to the writ set down from the source. Mother, father, brother, son and wife: among them God has joined (him). (He) himself causes deeds, and good deeds, to be done; nothing is in this creature's power. Says Nanak, O mortal, in the first watch (the Lord) gives (the soul) a place in the womb. O merchant friend, in the second watch of the night, youth at its full surges in waves. He does not tell bad from good, O merchant friend; the mind is drunk with ego. The mortal does not tell bad from good, (though) the road ahead is hard. He never served the perfect True Guru; the cruel Jams stand over his head. When Dharam Raj seizes the crazed one, what answer will he give then? Says Nanak, in the second watch the mortal's youth at its full surges in waves. O merchant friend, in the third watch of the night, one blind in ignorance hoards poison. Entangled in attachment to son and wife, O merchant friend, he has waves of greed within. With waves of greed within, the mortal does not bring that God to mind. He has kept no company with the Saadh Sangat; he suffers pain in many births. He has forgotten the Creator, the Master; not for an instant has (his) attention been fixed (on him). Says Nanak, in the third watch the mortal, blind in ignorance, hoards poison. O merchant friend, in the fourth watch of the night, that day has drawn near. Through the Guru, cherish the Naam, O merchant friend; it will be your friend in the Lord's court. Through the Guru, cherish the Naam, O mortal; at the end it will be your companion. This attachment and Maya will not go with you; it is a false love you have formed. The whole night has passed in darkness; serve the True Guru, and there will be light. Says Nanak, O mortal, in the fourth watch that day has drawn near. The written summons of Govind has come, O merchant friend; they rise and depart, with (only) their deeds for company. (Jam's messengers) allow not a moment's delay, O merchant friend; they have laid a firm hold. The summons came, and (they) seized and drove (him) off; the manmukhs are ever in misery. Those who served the perfect True Guru are ever at ease in the Lord's court. In this age the body is the field of deeds; whatever one sows, that one eats. Says Nanak, the devotees shine in (the Lord's) court; the manmukhs ever wander (through births). ॥5॥
78.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 2, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. How can the young, unknowing bride behold the sight of the Lord in her parents' home? (When) the Lord, Har Har, shows his grace, she learns through the Guru the tasks of her in-laws' home. Learning through the Guru the tasks of her in-laws' home, she ever meditates on the Lord, Har Har. Among her companions she moves at ease; in the Lord's court she walks free of care, swinging her arms. Repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, she clears what stands owing in Dharam Raj's account. Through the Guru, the young, unknowing bride beholds the sight of the Lord while still in her parents' home. My wedding has taken place, O my father; through the Guru I have found the Lord. The darkness of ignorance is cut away, for the Guru's blazing knowledge has been lit. The Guru's knowledge shone, the darkness perished, and I have found the Lord, the priceless jewel. The disease of Haumai is gone, the pain is lifted; through the Guru's teaching, the self has eaten up its own self-conceit. I have found as my husband the One whose form is beyond time, the Imperishable, who never dies and is never born. My wedding has taken place, O my father; through the Guru I have found the Lord. The Lord is true, ever true, O my father; with the Lord's servants gathered together, the wedding procession looks beautiful. Repeating the Lord('s Name) in her parents' home, (the bride) lives at ease, and in her in-laws' home she shines with true beauty. She shines with true beauty in her in-laws' home who has kept the Naam close in her parents' home. Wholly fruitful is the life of those who, through the Guru, have conquered the mind and then cast the dice (in the game of life). Joined by the Lord's Sants, the wedding was made beautiful; (she) has found as husband the all-pervading Being who is bliss itself. The Lord is true, ever true, O my father; with the Lord's servants gathered together, the wedding procession looks beautiful. O my father, give me the Lord God as my gift; give me the Lord as my dowry. Give me the Lord as my clothes, the Lord as my adornment, that my wedding may be made fair. Through devotion to the Lord, Har Har, the wedding becomes a joy; the Guru, the True Guru, has had this gift bestowed. In the land and through the universe there is glory through the Lord (given as dowry); no other gift, set beside it, can match this one. The dowry that other manmukhs lay out for show is false pride, a sham of glass. O my father, give me the Lord God as my gift; give me the Lord as my dowry. O my father, meeting her Husband, the Lord, Ram, the bride's vine (her line) spreads and grows. Age upon age, through every age, the line of the Guru, one with the Lord, goes on for ever. In every age the True Guru's line goes on: all those who have meditated on the Naam through the Guru. The Lord, the all-pervading Being, never perishes and never passes away; he gives each day, and (his giving) keeps on growing. O Nanak, the Sant and the Lord of the Sants are one; repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (the bride) shines in beauty. O my father, meeting her Husband, the Lord, Ram, the bride's vine (her line) spreads and grows. ॥5॥

Chhant: a song of longer stanzas. In this one the soul-bride speaks to her father (babul) as a daughter does at her wedding: the procession (janj), the dowry (daaj), the bridal clothes; the Husband is the Lord.
The bride's vine (vel) and the Guru's line (peerhee) are their descendants: all who, through them, come to meditate on the Name.
79.1: Sri Raag, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O dear mind, my friend, keep the Name of Gobind close within. O dear mind, my friend, the Lord will stand by you to the end. Meditate on the Lord's Name, your companion and helper; no one (who does) goes away empty-handed. Fixing your mind on the lotus feet (of the Lord), you will obtain the very fruits your heart longs for. Banwari, the Lord, fills water and land; dwelling in every heart, he watches over (all) with his gaze. Nanak gives this counsel, O beloved mind: in the Saadh Sangat, burn away your doubt. O dear mind, my friend, without the Lord all this expanse is false. O dear mind, my friend, this world is a sea of poison. Make the Creator's lotus feet your ship; then fear and pain cannot seize you. The one who, by great good fortune, meets the Perfect Guru repeats the Name of God at all hours. From the beginning, from the dawn of the ages, (God) is the Master (and keeper) of his servants; (his) Name is the support of the devotees. Nanak gives this counsel, O beloved mind: without the Lord all this expanse is false. O dear mind, my friend, load the cargo of the Lord('s Name), the cargo that brings gain. O dear mind, my friend, take your place at the Lord's door, the door that never moves. Whoever serves at the door of the Lord, unseen and unfathomable, gains a seat that never shakes. There is no birth, no death, no coming and going there; fear and pain are wiped away. The record of Chitr and Gupt is torn up, and Death's messengers have no power at all. Nanak gives this counsel, O beloved mind: load the cargo of the Lord('s Name), the cargo that brings gain. O dear mind, my friend, make your dwelling with the Sants. O dear mind, my friend, repeating the Lord's Name, light dawns (within). Remembering the Master, who brings peace, every desire is fulfilled. By what was earned before, Sri Rang (the Lord) is found; those long separated meet the Lord. Within and without, (the Lord) pervades everywhere: this faith springs up in the mind. Nanak gives this counsel, O beloved mind: make your dwelling with the Sants. O dear mind, my friend, (the one whose) mind is absorbed in loving devotion to the Lord, O dear mind, my friend, (that one) lives by meeting the Lord, as a fish lives by meeting water. Drinking the Amrit word of the Lord, they are fulfilled, and every comfort comes to dwell in (their) minds. They find Sridhar (the Lord) and sing songs of joy; the True Guru being pleased, (their) wish is fulfilled. (The Lord) has attached (them) to his hem; they have obtained the nine treasures: the Master gave (them) the Name, which is everything. O Nanak, (the one) whom the Sants have taught this counsel has a mind absorbed in loving devotion to the Lord. ॥5॥
Banwari (he of the forest garland), Sri Rang and Sridhar (the lord of Sri, Lakshmi, and he who holds her) are names of Vishnu; in Gurbani they are names of God.
Chitr and Gupt are, by tradition, the two recorders at Dharam Raj's court who write down the deeds of every being.
The nine treasures (nau nidh): in Puranic lore, the nine treasures of Kuber, the god of wealth; here, every kind of wealth.
80.1: Chhants of Sri Raag: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. My Beloved is within my very heart; how may I see him face to face? O Nanak, he who sustains the breath of life is found in the Sants' refuge. The way of love for the lotus feet (of the Lord) dwells in the minds of the Sants. Love of another, a perverse way, wrong conduct: these do not please (the Lord's) servants. These do not please the servants; without the sight (of the Lord), how could (a servant) keep patience even for a moment? Bereft of the Name, (his) body and mind waste away; he dies as a fish dies without water. Meet me, my Beloved, support of my breath, that (your servant) may join the Saadh Sangat and sing (your) virtues. O Master of Nanak, show your grace, that (Nanak) may stay merged, mind and body, in your embrace. (The Lord) is radiant in every place; no other is to be seen. O Nanak, on meeting the True Guru, the doors (of the mind) have opened. (O Lord), your words are beyond compare and without end, the support of the Sants; (your) Bani is to be reflected upon. Remembering (you) with every breath and morsel, in full faith, why should (you) be forgotten from the mind? Why should (you) be forgotten from the mind? Not for the twinkling of an eye should (you) be set aside: O Lord of all virtues, (you are) our very breath. The Master gives the fruits the mind desires, and tends the pain of every soul. O Master of the masterless, companion of all: repeating (your Name), one does not lose this life in a gamble. This is Nanak's prayer to God: in your grace, carry (me) across the world-ocean. Bathing in the dust (of the feet) of the holy (is granted) when the Lord becomes merciful. All good things are found, O Nanak, in the wealth and riches of the Lord('s Name). The home of the beautiful Master is the resting place of the devotees; in hope of it they live. Remembering God's Name, they are absorbed (in him) in mind and body, and drink the Amrit of the Lord. Drinking the Lord's Amrit, they become ever steady, and know the water of sense-pleasures to be tasteless. God, my Lord Gopal, has become merciful (to them), and in the Saadh Sangat their mind is content with the treasure (of the Name). (The Name is) their all, their peace and deep bliss; they keep the jewel of the beloved Lord sewn within their minds. Not for a moment do they forget the support of their breath; O Nanak, they live by repeating (his Name) over and over. (O Lord), those whom you have made your own, you have met. You yourself are enchanted; O Nanak, you yourself have heard your own praise (from them). Administering the drug of love and winning his favour, (the Sants) have captivated the heart of Gobind. By the grace of the Sants, (one) clings to the neck of the unfathomable (Lord) and is made beautiful. Clinging to the Lord's neck he is made beautiful, and all faults are driven off; by the marks of devotion, (the Lord) has come under (his) sway. All comforts have come to dwell in the mind, Govind being pleased, and births and deaths are all wiped away. With (holy) companions the song of joy was sung, the wish was fulfilled, and the jolts of Maya strike no more. O Nanak, those whom the beloved Lord has taken by the hand are not touched by the world-ocean. The Name of the Master is priceless; no one knows its worth. O Nanak, those with good fortune on their foreheads enjoy the love of the Lord. Those who speak (the Lord's praise) are pure, all who hear it are blessed, and those who write it have carried their families across. Those who have the company of the Saadh (the Guru) and the love of the Lord's Name have contemplated Brahm. Contemplating Brahm, they have made their life fair; God has shown them his full grace. Taking (them) by the hand, (God) has given them his praise; they no longer run through births, nor die. Meeting the kind and compassionate True Guru, they have grown green (with new life) and have slain lust, anger and greed. The indescribable Master cannot be described; Nanak is a sacrifice, devoted (to him). ॥5॥
Dakhna: a salok in the speech of south-western Punjab (around Multan), where ਡ often stands for ਦ (ਡੂਜੜੋ, second) and ਹ for ਸ (ਹਭ, all).
Bikhai ban: here ban (Sanskrit vana) is water, set against the Amrit the devotees drink.
81.1: Sri Raag, Vanjara, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); realised through the Guru's grace. Supreme is the Name of the Lord, Har Har, who created each and every one. The Lord sustains all beings; he, the all-pervading Lord, dwells in every heart. Let us meditate ever on that Lord; without him there is no other. Those who set their minds on attachment to Maya leave (it all) behind and depart, weeping in pain. O servant Nanak, (for those who) have meditated on the Naam, the Lord is a companion at the last. For me there is none but the Lord. The Lord is found in the Guru's refuge, O merchant friend; he is attained by great good fortune. Without the Sants, O brothers, no one has obtained the Name of the Lord. (Without them, people) do their deeds in Haumai, like a prostitute's son, who has no (father's) name. One comes to belong to the Father's (the Lord's) line only when the Guru, pleased, shows his grace. The one who has found the Guru by great good fortune is in love with the Lord day and night. Servant Nanak has recognised Brahm, by practising the deed of the Lord's praise. A longing for the Lord, Har Har, has risen in (my) mind. The Perfect Guru has fixed the Name firmly within; the Lord is found, the Name of the Lord God is found. As long as there is breath in your youth, so long meditate on the Name. When you depart, the Lord will go with you; at the last the Lord will set you free. I am a sacrifice to those in whose minds the Lord has come and settled. Those who did not remember the Name of the Lord, Har Har, went away at the last in regret. O servant Nanak, (the one on whose) forehead the Lord God wrote (it) from the beginning (alone) meditates on the Naam. O mind, fix your love on the Lord, Har Har. The one who by great good fortune has found the Guru, (the Lord) carries across through the Guru's Shabad. The Lord himself brings himself forth (as the world); the Lord himself gives (life) and takes it back. The Lord himself leads astray in doubt; the Lord himself gives understanding. In the minds of the Gurmukhs there is light; but they are rare, a very few. I am a sacrifice to those who have found the Lord through the Guru's teaching. Within servant Nanak the lotus (of the heart) has blossomed; the Lord, Har Har, has settled in the mind. (O soul), repeat the Lord's Name, Har Har, in your mind. Run to the refuge of the Lord and the Guru, O soul, and cast off all sins and sorrows. The all-pervading Lord dwells in every heart and mind; how is he to be found, and by what means? If one meets the Guru, the Perfect True Guru, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind and heart. For me the Name is the prop and the support; from the Lord's Name come (my) liberation and wisdom. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is my trust; in the Lord's Name alone are (my) caste and honour. Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam; he is dyed in love, steeped in the love of the Lord. Meditate on the Lord: the Lord God is true and ever abiding. Through the Guru's word the Lord God is known; all creation comes from the Lord God. Those for whom it was written from before come and meet the Guru. In those who come in the spirit of servants, O merchant friend, the Guru makes the Name of the Lord, Har Har, shine forth. Blessed, blessed is the dealing of the traders whose loaded merchandise is the capital of the Lord('s Name). Bright are the faces of the Gurmukhs at (the Lord's) door; they come and meet the Lord. O servant Nanak, the Guru is found by those with whom the treasure of virtues, (the Lord) himself, is pleased. With every breath and every morsel, meditate on the Lord. Love has sprung up in the minds of those Gurmukhs for whom the Lord's Name is the provision for life's road. ॥1॥
In this hymn (Vanjara, the merchant) each stanza is followed by its own two-line Rahao (Pause).
83.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Sri Raag ki Vaar: by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji), with saloks. Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Among the ragas, Sri Raag is (the highest) only if through it one sets (one's) love on the True One. (Then) the True Lord, the Infinite, dwells in the mind for ever, and the understanding grows steady. (Such a one) has found a priceless jewel: reflection on the Guru's Shabad. (That one's) tongue becomes true, the mind true, and the whole frame of the body true. O Nanak, when the True Guru, the true one, is served, the trade (one does) is true for ever. ॥1॥
A vaar is a hymn of pauris (stanzas); in this vaar the pauris are the Fourth Guru's, and each pauri is preceded by saloks of the Gurus, the number after ਮਃ (Mahla) naming the Guru who wrote each one.
Apaaru (masculine, with aunkar) describes the Lord, not mati (understanding, feminine).
83.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). So long as there is no love for the Master, every other love is only the restless chase of Maya. Lured by Maya, this mind can neither see (the Lord) nor hear (him). Without seeing the Husband, love does not spring up; what can the blind (mind) do? O Nanak, the True One who took the eyes away is the one who gives (them back). ॥2॥
83.3: The Lord alone is the Creator, the One; the Lord alone holds the one court. The command is the One Lord's alone; keep that One Lord in your mind. Apart from that Lord there is no one; so put away your fear, your doubt and your dread. Praise that Lord alone, who keeps you safe out of doors and at home. The one on whom the Lord is merciful repeats the Lord's Name and crosses the hard sea of fear. ॥1॥
83.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The gifts are the Master's; what force can prevail against him? Some, though awake, do not find (them), and others he wakes from their sleep and gives (them). ॥1॥
Sandeeaa: of, belonging to (a Lahndi genitive).
83.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Faith and contentment are the wealth of the faithful, and patience is the provision the angels (the godly) carry for the road. They obtain the sight of the Perfect One; for the idle talkers there is no place. ॥2॥

This salok is in Persian and Arabic words: sidak (faith), sabooree (contentment, thankfulness), saadik (the faithful), sabar (patience), tosaa (provisions for a journey), malaaik (angels), khaaik (idle talkers).
83.6: (O Lord,) you yourself brought forth all (creation), and you yourself set it to its work. You yourself look on your own greatness and rejoice. O Lord, nothing is outside you; you are the True Master. You yourself, you alone, are at work in every place. O Sants, meditate on that Lord alone, who sets free. ॥2॥
83.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Empty is (pride of) caste, empty (pride of) a name. Over all beings there is one shade, (the one Lord's). If someone has himself called good on his own account, O Nanak, (he) is truly known (as good) only when he wins honour in the (Lord's) reckoning. ॥1॥
83.8: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). The Beloved whom one loves: before him one should die (to self). Cursed is the life lived in the world with one's back turned on him. ॥2॥
83.9: (O Lord,) you yourself fashioned the earth, and the moon and the sun, two lamps. You made fourteen shops (worlds) for the trade to be done. To some the Lord gives profit: those who become Gurmukh. Jamkaal has no hold on those who have drunk the true Amrit. They themselves are set free, with their families, and following them the whole world is set free. ॥3॥
The fourteen shops: the fourteen worlds of Puranic count (seven above, seven below), which the Guru calls shops, where beings have come to trade (in the Name).
83.10: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Having made the creation, he himself dwells (in it). The one who weighs the worth of (this human) time becomes (his) servant. (God) is in (his) creation, (yet his) worth cannot be reckoned. Even if (someone) reckoned it, (it) could not be told. (Those who) ponder (only) the shara and the shariat, how will they reach the far shore without understanding (the real)? Make faith your sijda, and make the joining of the mind (to God) your aim. (Then) whichever way I look, there (God) is present. ॥1॥
Shara and shariat: the religious law of Islam and its rules; sijda: the prostration of the namaz, the forehead to the ground; makhsood: aim, purpose.
84.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Guru's company is not had in this way, by being (bodily) near or far. O Nanak, the True Guru is met when the mind stays in (his) presence. ॥2॥
84.2: The seven continents and the seven seas, the nine regions, the four Vedas and the eighteen Puranas: O Lord, you are at work in all of these; O Lord, you are dear to all. Every being and creature meditates on you, O Lord Saringpani. Those who worship the Lord through the Guru: to them I am a sacrifice. Staging wondrous plays, you yourself, you alone, are at work (in all). ॥4॥
The seven continents (deep), the seven seas and the nine regions (khand): the earth as the Puranas divide it.
84.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Why send for pen and inkpot? Write (the Lord's Name) in the heart itself. (So one) stays ever dyed in the Master's love, and (that) love never breaks. Pen and inkpot will pass away, and what was written goes with them. O Nanak, love for the Husband will not pass away, which the True One placed (in the heart) from the very first. ॥1॥
84.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). What can be seen does not go along (with anyone); let anyone weigh it and see. The True Guru has made the Truth firm (within): keep your attention fixed on the True One. O Nanak, the True One is (found) through the Shabad; by (his) grace (he) comes into one's keeping. ॥2॥
84.5: O Lord, within and without, you alone are; you know the secret (of every heart). Whatever is done, the Lord knows; O my mind, remember the Lord. He who commits sins is afraid; the righteous one blossoms. (O Lord,) true are you yourself, and true (your) justice; why then should one fear? O Nanak, those who have recognised the True One blend into the True One. ॥5॥
84.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Let (that) pen burn, along with the inkpot, and let (that) paper burn too; let the writer burn up as well, who has written (only) the love of another. O Nanak, (one) must act out what was written from before; nothing else can be done. ॥1॥
84.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Other reading (than the Name) is false, (other) speaking is false: (it is) love of Maya. O Nanak, without the Name nothing lasts; reading and reading (only these), one is ruined. ॥2॥
84.8: Great is the Lord's glory; (great is) the Kirtan of the Lord. Great is the Lord's glory, for (his) justice is the justice of righteousness. Great is the Lord's glory, for each being (receives) the fruit (of its own deeds). Great is the Lord's glory, for he does not listen to the backbiter's word. Great is the Lord's glory, (for) he bestows (his) gifts without consulting (anyone). ॥6॥
84.9: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Crying I, I, all (the world) has died away; wealth (goes) with no one. In the love of another (all) have suffered pain; Jamkaal has its eye on all (the world). O Nanak, the Gurmukhs have come through safe, cherishing the True Name. ॥1॥
85.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In words we (brides) are good, but in our conduct bad. Within the mind we are impure and black, (yet) white outside. We copy those who stand (alert) at (the Lord's) door and serve, (who,) dyed in their Master's love, enjoy delights in peace, (and who,) though they have strength, live as the powerless and the humble. O Nanak, (our) life (would be) fruitful if we joined their company. ॥2॥
85.2: (O God,) you are yourself the water and yourself the fish; you yourself, you alone, are the net. You yourself spread the net, and you yourself are the green moss in (the water). You yourself are the lotus, untouched (by the water), glowing red in (water) hundreds of cubits deep. You yourself bring liberation to (whoever) gives thought (to you) for an instant, a moment. O Lord, nothing is outside you; seeing (you everywhere) through the Guru's Shabad, (the mind) is filled with joy. ॥7॥
Sebaal (Sanskrit shaivala): the green moss that forms on water.
85.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (The soul-bride) who does not understand (the Lord's) Hukam weeps much. With anxiety within (her), she does not sleep (a restful) sleep. If the soul-bride walks in her Master's will, she is honoured at (his) door and in (her own) home, and is called into (his) mansion. O Nanak, by (the Lord's) grace this understanding is received, (and) by the Guru's grace (the soul-bride) merges in the True One. ॥1॥
85.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O manmukh, empty of the Name, do not be led astray by the sight of the safflower's colour. Its colour lasts a few days; its worth is trifling. Clinging to another, the foolish, the blind and the ignorant waste away and die. They are worms in filth, falling into it to rot again and again. O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam are bright with colour; through the Guru they abide in Sahaj and in love. (Their) colour of devotion does not fade; (they) remain merged in Sahaj. ॥2॥
85.5: (O Lord,) you brought forth all the world, and you yourself have brought (all) their sustenance. Some eat by trickery and deceit; they spill falsehood and untruth from their lips. What pleases you yourself, that they do; you have set them to that very work. To some he has given understanding of the Truth, (and) to them he has had storehouses given that never run short. Those who eat remembering the Lord: for them (it) bears fruit; the heedless (of him) are left with hands held out (to beg). ॥8॥
85.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Reading and reading, the pandits expound the Vedas, (but) for the taste of attachment to Maya. In the love of another (they) have forgotten the Lord's Name; (such) a foolish mind receives punishment. He never remembers the One who gave him soul and body, who brings him his sustenance and gives it. The noose of Jam is not cut from (his) neck; again and again he comes and goes. The manmukh can see nothing; the blind one acts out what was written from before. By perfect fortune the True Guru, giver of peace, is met, (and) the Naam comes to dwell in the mind. (Such ones) enjoy peace and wear peace, (and their life) passes in peace upon peace. O Nanak, let us not forget from the mind that Name through which glory is won at the true door. ॥1॥
85.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Serving the True Guru, (that one) has found peace: the True Name, the treasure of virtues. Through the Guru's teaching (that one) has recognised the self, (and within is) the light of the Name of Ram. (That one) practises Truth and Truth alone, (and) is given glory in the presence of the Great One. Soul and body, all are his (God's); (knowing this, that one) praises (him) and prays (to him). Praising (the Lord) through the true Shabad, one dwells in peace upon peace. (For that one) chanting, austerity and self-restraint lie within the mind; without the Name, life is cursed. The Name is obtained through the Guru's teaching; the manmukh perishes in attachment. (O God,) keep (me) as it pleases you; Nanak is your servant. ॥2॥
86.1: (O Lord,) everyone is yours, and you are everyone's; you are the capital of all. All ask of you alone, praying day after day. The one to whom you give receives everything; from some you are far, though (ever) near. Apart from you there is no place to ask from; let anyone weigh it in the mind and see. All praise you; at your door you bring the Gurmukhs into the light. ॥9॥
86.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The pandit reads and reads (the scriptures) and calls them out aloud, but his love lies in attachment to Maya. He does not recognise God within; at heart he is a fool, unlettered. Caught in the love of another, he instructs the world, yet does not grasp the reflection himself. He has wasted his life in vain; he dies and is born, time after time. ॥1॥
86.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who served the True Guru obtained the Name; reflect on this and understand. Calm and peace dwell in their minds for ever, and their crying and wailing come to an end. Through reflection on the Guru's Shabad, the self devours its own self-conceit, and the mind becomes pure. O Nanak, those steeped in the Shabad are liberated; they bear affection and love for the dear Lord. ॥2॥
86.4: Service of the Lord bears fruit; the Gurmukh's (service) is accepted. One who is pleasing to the Lord meets the Guru, and he meditates on the Lord's Name. Through the Guru's Shabad the Lord is found, and the Lord carries (one) across. No one has found (him) by the stubbornness of the mind; go and ask the Vedas. O Nanak, the Lord's service is done only by one whom the Lord himself sets to it. ॥10॥
86.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O Nanak, he is the brave warrior who has slain the wicked ego within. Praising the Naam through the Guru, he has made his life beautiful. He himself is liberated for ever, and he has carried his whole lineage across. Those who love the Naam are radiant at the door of the True One. The manmukhs die in ego; they have spoiled even their death. (God's) Hukam alone is at work in everything; what can the poor creatures do? Straying from their own self and clinging to another, they have forgotten the Master. O Nanak, without the Name all is pain, and peace is forgotten. ॥1॥
86.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One in whom the perfect Guru has made the Lord's Name firm has driven doubt from within. He has sung the Name of Ram and the Lord's praise, and, making it a light, (the Guru) has shown him the way. Having slain Haumai, he is lovingly attuned to the One, and has enshrined the Naam within. Through the Guru's teaching Jam cannot even cast an eye on him; he has merged in the True Name. The Creator himself is at work in all; whoever pleases him, he attaches to the Name. Servant Nanak lives when he takes the Name; without the Name he dies in an instant. ॥2॥
