The one on whom the Lord is merciful repeats the Lord's Name and crosses the hard sea of fear. ॥1॥
83.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The gifts are the Master's; what force can prevail against him?
Some, though awake, do not find (them), and others he wakes from their sleep and gives (them). ॥1॥
83.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Faith and contentment are the wealth of the faithful, and patience is the provision the angels (the godly) carry for the road.
They obtain the sight of the Perfect One; for the idle talkers there is no place. ॥2॥
83.6: (O Lord,) you yourself brought forth all (creation), and you yourself set it to its work.
You yourself look on your own greatness and rejoice.
O Lord, nothing is outside you; you are the True Master.
You yourself, you alone, are at work in every place.
O Sants, meditate on that Lord alone, who sets free. ॥2॥
83.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Empty is (pride of) caste, empty (pride of) a name.
Over all beings there is one shade, (the one Lord's).
If someone has himself called good on his own account,
O Nanak, (he) is truly known (as good) only when he wins honour in the (Lord's) reckoning. ॥1॥
83.8: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The Beloved whom one loves: before him one should die (to self).
Cursed is the life lived in the world with one's back turned on him. ॥2॥
83.9: (O Lord,) you yourself fashioned the earth, and the moon and the sun, two lamps.
You made fourteen shops (worlds) for the trade to be done.
To some the Lord gives profit: those who become Gurmukh.
Jamkaal has no hold on those who have drunk the true Amrit.
They themselves are set free, with their families, and following them the whole world is set free. ॥3॥
83.10: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Having made the creation, he himself dwells (in it).
The one who weighs the worth of (this human) time becomes (his) servant.
(God) is in (his) creation, (yet his) worth cannot be reckoned.
Even if (someone) reckoned it, (it) could not be told.
(Those who) ponder (only) the shara and the shariat,
how will they reach the far shore without understanding (the real)?
Make faith your sijda, and make the joining of the mind (to God) your aim.
(Then) whichever way I look, there (God) is present. ॥1॥
84.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Guru's company is not had in this way, by being (bodily) near or far.
O Nanak, the True Guru is met when the mind stays in (his) presence. ॥2॥
84.2: The seven continents and the seven seas, the nine regions, the four Vedas and the eighteen Puranas:
O Lord, you are at work in all of these; O Lord, you are dear to all.
Every being and creature meditates on you, O Lord Saringpani.
Those who worship the Lord through the Guru: to them I am a sacrifice.
Staging wondrous plays, you yourself, you alone, are at work (in all). ॥4॥
84.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Why send for pen and inkpot? Write (the Lord's Name) in the heart itself.
(So one) stays ever dyed in the Master's love, and (that) love never breaks.
Pen and inkpot will pass away, and what was written goes with them.
O Nanak, love for the Husband will not pass away, which the True One placed (in the heart) from the very first. ॥1॥
84.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
What can be seen does not go along (with anyone); let anyone weigh it and see.
The True Guru has made the Truth firm (within): keep your attention fixed on the True One.
O Nanak, the True One is (found) through the Shabad; by (his) grace (he) comes into one's keeping. ॥2॥
84.5: O Lord, within and without, you alone are; you know the secret (of every heart).
Whatever is done, the Lord knows; O my mind, remember the Lord.
He who commits sins is afraid; the righteous one blossoms.
(O Lord,) true are you yourself, and true (your) justice; why then should one fear?
O Nanak, those who have recognised the True One blend into the True One. ॥5॥
84.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Let (that) pen burn, along with the inkpot, and let (that) paper burn too;
let the writer burn up as well, who has written (only) the love of another.
O Nanak, (one) must act out what was written from before; nothing else can be done. ॥1॥
84.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Other reading (than the Name) is false, (other) speaking is false: (it is) love of Maya.
O Nanak, without the Name nothing lasts; reading and reading (only these), one is ruined. ॥2॥
84.8: Great is the Lord's glory; (great is) the Kirtan of the Lord.
Great is the Lord's glory, for (his) justice is the justice of righteousness.
Great is the Lord's glory, for each being (receives) the fruit (of its own deeds).
Great is the Lord's glory, for he does not listen to the backbiter's word.
Great is the Lord's glory, (for) he bestows (his) gifts without consulting (anyone). ॥6॥
84.9: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Crying I, I, all (the world) has died away; wealth (goes) with no one.
In the love of another (all) have suffered pain; Jamkaal has its eye on all (the world).
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs have come through safe, cherishing the True Name. ॥1॥
85.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In words we (brides) are good, but in our conduct bad.
Within the mind we are impure and black, (yet) white outside.
We copy those who stand (alert) at (the Lord's) door and serve,
(who,) dyed in their Master's love, enjoy delights in peace,
(and who,) though they have strength, live as the powerless and the humble.
O Nanak, (our) life (would be) fruitful if we joined their company. ॥2॥
85.2: (O God,) you are yourself the water and yourself the fish; you yourself, you alone, are the net.
You yourself spread the net, and you yourself are the green moss in (the water).
You yourself are the lotus, untouched (by the water), glowing red in (water) hundreds of cubits deep.
You yourself bring liberation to (whoever) gives thought (to you) for an instant, a moment.
O Lord, nothing is outside you; seeing (you everywhere) through the Guru's Shabad, (the mind) is filled with joy. ॥7॥
85.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The soul-bride) who does not understand (the Lord's) Hukam weeps much.
With anxiety within (her), she does not sleep (a restful) sleep.
If the soul-bride walks in her Master's will,
she is honoured at (his) door and in (her own) home, and is called into (his) mansion.
O Nanak, by (the Lord's) grace this understanding is received,
(and) by the Guru's grace (the soul-bride) merges in the True One. ॥1॥
85.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O manmukh, empty of the Name, do not be led astray by the sight of the safflower's colour.
Its colour lasts a few days; its worth is trifling.
Clinging to another, the foolish, the blind and the ignorant waste away and die.
They are worms in filth, falling into it to rot again and again.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam are bright with colour; through the Guru they abide in Sahaj and in love.
(Their) colour of devotion does not fade; (they) remain merged in Sahaj. ॥2॥
85.5: (O Lord,) you brought forth all the world, and you yourself have brought (all) their sustenance.
Some eat by trickery and deceit; they spill falsehood and untruth from their lips.
What pleases you yourself, that they do; you have set them to that very work.
To some he has given understanding of the Truth, (and) to them he has had storehouses given that never run short.
Those who eat remembering the Lord: for them (it) bears fruit; the heedless (of him) are left with hands held out (to beg). ॥8॥
85.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Reading and reading, the pandits expound the Vedas, (but) for the taste of attachment to Maya.
In the love of another (they) have forgotten the Lord's Name; (such) a foolish mind receives punishment.
He never remembers the One who gave him soul and body, who brings him his sustenance and gives it.
The noose of Jam is not cut from (his) neck; again and again he comes and goes.
The manmukh can see nothing; the blind one acts out what was written from before.
By perfect fortune the True Guru, giver of peace, is met, (and) the Naam comes to dwell in the mind.
(Such ones) enjoy peace and wear peace, (and their life) passes in peace upon peace.
O Nanak, let us not forget from the mind that Name through which glory is won at the true door. ॥1॥
85.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Serving the True Guru, (that one) has found peace: the True Name, the treasure of virtues.
Through the Guru's teaching (that one) has recognised the self, (and within is) the light of the Name of Ram.
(That one) practises Truth and Truth alone, (and) is given glory in the presence of the Great One.
Soul and body, all are his (God's); (knowing this, that one) praises (him) and prays (to him).
Praising (the Lord) through the true Shabad, one dwells in peace upon peace.
(For that one) chanting, austerity and self-restraint lie within the mind; without the Name, life is cursed.
The Name is obtained through the Guru's teaching; the manmukh perishes in attachment.
(O God,) keep (me) as it pleases you; Nanak is your servant. ॥2॥
86.1: (O Lord,) everyone is yours, and you are everyone's; you are the capital of all.
All ask of you alone, praying day after day.
The one to whom you give receives everything; from some you are far, though (ever) near.
Apart from you there is no place to ask from; let anyone weigh it in the mind and see.
All praise you; at your door you bring the Gurmukhs into the light. ॥9॥
86.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The pandit reads and reads (the scriptures) and calls them out aloud, but his love lies in attachment to Maya.
He does not recognise God within; at heart he is a fool, unlettered.
Caught in the love of another, he instructs the world, yet does not grasp the reflection himself.
He has wasted his life in vain; he dies and is born, time after time. ॥1॥
86.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who served the True Guru obtained the Name; reflect on this and understand.
Calm and peace dwell in their minds for ever, and their crying and wailing come to an end.
Through reflection on the Guru's Shabad, the self devours its own self-conceit, and the mind becomes pure.
O Nanak, those steeped in the Shabad are liberated; they bear affection and love for the dear Lord. ॥2॥
86.4: Service of the Lord bears fruit; the Gurmukh's (service) is accepted.
One who is pleasing to the Lord meets the Guru, and he meditates on the Lord's Name.
Through the Guru's Shabad the Lord is found, and the Lord carries (one) across.
No one has found (him) by the stubbornness of the mind; go and ask the Vedas.
O Nanak, the Lord's service is done only by one whom the Lord himself sets to it. ॥10॥
86.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, he is the brave warrior who has slain the wicked ego within.
Praising the Naam through the Guru, he has made his life beautiful.
He himself is liberated for ever, and he has carried his whole lineage across.
Those who love the Naam are radiant at the door of the True One.
The manmukhs die in ego; they have spoiled even their death.
(God's) Hukam alone is at work in everything; what can the poor creatures do?
Straying from their own self and clinging to another, they have forgotten the Master.
O Nanak, without the Name all is pain, and peace is forgotten. ॥1॥
86.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One in whom the perfect Guru has made the Lord's Name firm has driven doubt from within.
He has sung the Name of Ram and the Lord's praise, and, making it a light, (the Guru) has shown him the way.
Having slain Haumai, he is lovingly attuned to the One, and has enshrined the Naam within.
Through the Guru's teaching Jam cannot even cast an eye on him; he has merged in the True Name.
The Creator himself is at work in all; whoever pleases him, he attaches to the Name.
Servant Nanak lives when he takes the Name; without the Name he dies in an instant. ॥2॥
87.1: One who has been received at the Lord's court is received in every court.
Wherever he goes, there his face is bright with honour; at the sight of his face all sinners are carried across.
Within him is the treasure of the Naam, and the Naam alone surrounds him.
Let the Name be worshipped, let the Name be trusted; through the Name all sins are taken away.
Those who have meditated on the Naam with one mind and one heart have become steadfast in the world. ॥11॥
87.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Let the Divine Self be worshipped, in the Sahaj and the love the Guru gives.
When the soul comes to have faith in the Supreme Soul, it finds intimacy (with him) in its own home.
Through love for the Guru, of its own accord, the soul becomes steady and does not waver.
Without the Guru, Sahaj does not come, nor does greed's filth leave from within.
If the Lord's Name dwells in the mind for a moment, an instant, it is (as if) one has bathed at all the sixty-eight tiraths.
No filth clings to one who is joined to the True One; filth clings through the love of another.
It does not come off at all with washing, even if one bathes at the sixty-eight tiraths.
The manmukh does his deeds in ego, and earns nothing but pain upon pain.
O Nanak, the soiled (mind) becomes clean only when one merges in the True Guru. ॥1॥
87.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Counsel a manmukh as you may, when can he be made to understand?
Though brought in among (the Gurmukhs), the manmukh does not blend in; driven by the deeds he has done, he wanders.
Loving attention (to God) and the running after Maya are two paths; one does one's work by (the Lord's) Hukam.
The Gurmukh has subdued his mind, testing it on the touchstone of the Shabad.
He quarrels with the mind alone, holds council (sath) with the mind alone, and merges within the mind itself.
Through the True Shabad, in love, the mind obtains whatever it desires.
Let us ever partake of the nectar of the Naam, doing the work (of the Name) through the Guru.
Whoever battles with others, and not with his own mind, will depart having wasted his life.
Self-willed and stubborn of mind, the manmukh has lost (the game of life), practising falsehood and deceit.
By the Guru's grace (the Gurmukh) conquers the mind and fixes loving attention on the Lord.
O Nanak, the Gurmukh practises Truth; the manmukh keeps coming and going. ॥2॥
87.4: O Sants of the Lord, O brothers, hear a teaching of the True Guru, who is one with the Lord.
One on whose face and forehead good fortune is written from the start has taken (this teaching) and kept it in the heart.
The Lord's nectar-sweet discourse, sublime and supreme, (that person) has tasted with ease through the Guru's words.
There (within) light has dawned and the darkness is gone, as the sun draws away the night.
The Lord who is unseen, beyond the senses, beyond knowing and without stain has been seen with the eyes, through the Guru. ॥12॥
87.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who serves his True Guru puts his head (his life) to good account.
Such ones shed self-conceit from within, and remain lovingly attuned to the True One.
Those who have not served the True Guru have wasted their lives in vain.
O Nanak, he does whatever pleases him; nothing can be said (about it). ॥1॥
88.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The mind hemmed in by vices does only the deeds of vice.
The ignorant worship in the love of another, and in the Lord's court they meet punishment.
Let the Divine Self be worshipped; (but) without the True Guru one gains no understanding.
(To accept) the True Guru's will is chanting, austerity and self-restraint; by (God's) grace alone it comes into one's hands.
O Nanak, service is to be done with the attention held (in the Guru's will); whatever pleases the Lord is accepted. ॥2॥
88.2: O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, by which there is peace always, day and night.
O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in remembering which all sins and wrongs are washed away.
O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, by which poverty, pain and hunger all depart.
O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, by which love for the foremost of the Gurmukhs, (the Guru,) takes hold.
On whatever face the True One has written good fortune from the start, through that mouth the Lord has (his) Name repeated. ॥13॥
88.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have not served the True Guru, nor reflected through the Shabad,
within whom spiritual wisdom has not come, are as the dead in the world.
They are caught in the round of the eighty-four lakh forms of life; they die and are born again, and are ruined.
Only one whom the Lord himself moves to it serves the True Guru.
In the True Guru is the treasure of the Naam; it is obtained by (God's) grace.
Those steeped in the True One through the Guru's Shabad have loving attention that stays ever true.
O Nanak, one whom (the Lord) unites (with himself) is not parted (again); he merges in Sahaj. ॥1॥
88.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
He is a Bhagauti, (a true devotee of Bhagavan,) who knows the Lord,
and by the Guru's grace recognises his own self.
He holds back the wandering (mind) and brings it to the one home (within).
He dies while living, and utters the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, he merges in the True One. ॥2॥
88.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who has deceit within and calls himself a Bhagauti
will never find the Supreme Lord through such hypocrisy.
He slanders others, and smears filth on his own inner self.
He washes off the filth outside, but the defilement of the mind does not go.
He stirs up strife with the Sat Sangat.
Engrossed in the love of another, he is miserable day and night.
He does not remember the Lord's Name, and performs many rites.
What is written from before cannot be erased.
O Nanak, liberation is not found without serving the True Guru. ॥3॥
88.6: Those who have meditated on the True Guru do not fret and grieve, morning after morning.
Those who have meditated on the True Guru are content and wholly fulfilled.
Those who have meditated on the True Guru have no fear of Jam.
Those to whom the Lord has shown mercy fall at the True Guru's feet.
Their faces shine here and hereafter, and they go to the Lord's court robed in honour. ॥14॥
89.1: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The head that does not bow to the Master: let that head be cast away.
O Nanak, the body's cage that holds no pang of separation (from the Lord): take that cage and burn it. ॥1॥
89.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Strayed from the Root (the Creator), O Nanak, (the soul-bride) is born and dies over and over.
Deluded into taking (filth) for musk, she has fallen into a foul pit. ॥2॥
89.3: O my mind, let us meditate on such a Name of the Lord, who makes his command run over all.
O my mind, let us repeat such a Name of the Lord, who sets one free at the final hour.
O my mind, let us repeat such a Name of the Lord, which takes away all the mind's thirst and hunger.
The fortunate have repeated that Name through the Guru; (the Lord) has brought all slanderers and wicked ones to fall at their feet.
O Nanak, contemplate the Naam, the greatest of all; (the Lord) has brought all and made them bow before the Name. ॥15॥
89.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The ugly woman of ill conduct, false and counterfeit of mind, decks herself in fine dress;
she does not walk in her Husband's will; the foolish one gives the orders (herself).
She who walks in the Guru's will becomes able to drive away all her pain.
What the Creator has written from the start cannot be erased.
(The virtuous bride) surrenders mind and body to her Husband Lord, and sets her love on the Shabad.
Without the Name no one has found (him); reflect in your heart and see.
O Nanak, she alone is lovely and of good conduct in whom the Creator has taken delight. ॥1॥
89.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Attachment to Maya is pitch darkness; neither its near shore nor its far shore can be seen.
The ignorant manmukhs suffer great pain; forgetting the Lord's Name, they drown.
Rising each morning, they perform many rites, (but) their love is caught in the love of another.
Those who serve their True Guru reach the far shore of the terrifying world-ocean.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs, enshrining the True Name in the heart, merge in the True One. ॥2॥
89.6: The Lord fills the water, the land and the sky; besides him there is none.
The Lord himself sits and does justice, and strikes down and drives out all the false.
To the truthful he gives honour; the Lord has done righteous justice.
All of you, sing the praise of the Lord, who has kept the poor and the helpless safe.
He has made the righteous acclaimed, and has given punishment to the sinner. ॥16॥
89.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh is (like) a soiled woman, of ill conduct, a wicked wife,
who has left her own Husband at home and loves another man.
Her craving never ends; burning (in it), she cries out.
O Nanak, without the Name she is ugly and unlovely; her Husband has forsaken and abandoned her. ॥1॥
90.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The happy soul-bride is steeped in the Shabad, in love and affection for the True Guru.
With true love and affection she ever enjoys union with her own Husband.
Most lovely is that bride, beautiful and full of glory.
O Nanak, through the Name the Uniter has united the happy soul-bride (with himself). ॥2॥
90.2: O Lord, all sing your praise, you who have freed those who were caught.
O Lord, all bow before you, you who have kept (them) from sin.
O Lord, you are the honour of those who have none; O Lord, you are mightier than the mighty.
The Lord strikes down the proud and humbles them, and brings the foolish manmukhs into line.
To his devotees, the humble and the forlorn, the Lord grants glory. ॥17॥
90.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who walks in the will of the True Guru is granted great glory.
The sublime Name of the Lord comes to dwell in (his) mind, and no one can erase it.
The one on whom (God) bestows his grace receives (the Name) through his mercy.
O Nanak, the cause (of this) lies in the Creator's power; only a rare one understands (it) through the Guru. ॥1॥
90.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, those who have worshipped the Lord's Name, their attention held on the Lord night and day in one unbroken thread:
Maya, the Master's handmaid, works in service before them.
The Perfect (Guru) has made them perfect, by the Hukam of the One who adorns.
Whoever has understood (the Hukam) by the Guru's grace has found the door of liberation.
The manmukhs do not know the Hukam; the cruel Jam strikes them.
Those who have worshipped (him) through the Guru have crossed the terrifying world-ocean.
(The Guru) has wiped out all their faults with virtues; the Guru himself is the Forgiver. ॥2॥
90.5: The devotees put their trust in the Lord: the Lord knows everything.
None knows as fully as the Lord; the Lord weighs what is right (and judges).
Why should we fret and worry, when he strikes no one unjustly?
The Master is true, and true is his justice; it is the sinful man who loses.
O devotees, praise (him) with folded hands; the Lord carries his humble devotees across. ॥18॥
90.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
May I stay united with my Beloved, and keep (him) within, enshrined in my heart;
may I praise that God for ever and ever, in love and affection for the Guru.
O Nanak, the one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace he unites (with himself); she alone is the happy soul-bride. ॥1॥
90.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through service of the Guru the Lord is found, by the one on whom he casts his glance of grace.
From humans they became gods, meditating on the Name of the Lord.
Killing their Haumai, he united them (with himself); through the Guru's Shabad they crossed over.
O Nanak, the Lord, showing his own grace, has absorbed them in Sahaj. ॥2॥
90.8: Having (his devotees) perform his devotion, the Lord has shown forth his glory.
He himself makes (them) trust in him, and he himself has had (them) toil in his service.
The Lord gives bliss to his devotees, and he has seated them, steady, in their own home (within).
The sinners he does not let stay steady; he has picked them out and driven them into dreadful hell.
The Lord gives his love to his devotees; taking their side, he has delivered them. ॥19॥
91.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Evil intellect is the dumni (the minstrel woman), cruelty the butcher woman, slander of others in the heart the sweeper woman, and (the soul) is robbed by wrath, the chandal woman.
What comes of drawing lines (around the cooking square), when these four sit there with you?
Truth their discipline, good conduct their lines, the Name they repeat their bath:
O Nanak, hereafter they alone are exalted who give no counsel of sin. ॥1॥
91.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Be it swan or crane, what does it matter, when he casts his glance of grace on it?
If it pleases him, O Nanak, he makes a swan out of a crow. ॥2॥
91.3: Whatever task one wants done, let it be put before the Lord.
He sets the task right: this is the truth, on the True Guru's testimony.
In the company of the Sants the treasure, the nectar (of the Name), is tasted.
(Pray:) O merciful Destroyer of fear, protect your servant.
O Nanak, by singing the Lord's praises the unseen God is perceived. ॥20॥
91.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Soul and body, all is his; he gives support to all.
O Nanak, through the Guru let us serve the Giver for ever and ever.
I am a sacrifice to those who have meditated on the Lord, the Formless One.
Their faces are ever bright, and all the world bows before them. ॥1॥
91.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When the True Guru is met, (the mind) turns back (from Maya), and the nine treasures are there to spend and to eat.
The eighteen Siddhis follow (him) about, (but) he dwells in his own home, his own true place.
The unstruck melodies ever play (within him), and in the state of unman (the mind raised above the world) he keeps his attention fixed on the Lord.
O Nanak, devotion to the Lord dwells in the minds of those on whose foreheads (this) was written from the very beginning. ॥2॥
91.6: I am a minstrel (dhadhi) of the Lord God, my Master; I have come to the Lord's door.
Within (his court) the Lord heard (my) cry, and brought the minstrel before his face.
Calling the minstrel, the Lord asked: For what purpose have you come?
(I said:) O merciful God, give me always this gift, that I meditate on the Lord's Name.
The Lord, the Giver, had (me) repeat the Lord's Name, and robed Nanak (in honour).
91.7: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Sri Raag, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji; to be sung in the ghar of Ek Suaan.
The mother thinks her son is growing big; she does not see even this much, that day by day his span of life grows shorter.
Calling him mine, mine, she lavishes her fondness on him, and the King of Death watches and laughs.
(O Lord,) into such delusion you have cast the world.
How can it understand, when Maya has bewitched it?
Says Kabir: give up the pleasures of Maya's poison; in this company death (of the soul) is certain.
O mortal, repeat (the Name of) the all-pervading Lord; (his praise is) the word of everlasting life; in this way the world-ocean is crossed.
When it pleases him, then love (for him) takes hold,
and doubt and delusion leave from within.
Sahaj wells up, and the intellect wakes to wisdom;
by the Guru's grace, the attention is fixed (on God) within.
In this company (with the Lord) there is no death;
recognising his Hukam, one then meets the Master.
92.1: Sri Raag, the hymn of Bhagat Trilochan Ji.
O mortal, great is the love of Maya in (your) mind; you have forgotten the fear of old age and death.
Seeing your family you blossom like the lotus; you eye other people's homes, O man of deceit.
The sons of Jam (Death's messengers) come running;
before them I cannot hold my ground.
Only some rare friend (of God) comes and says:
Meet me, my Beethal; put your arms around me and take me (to you).
Meet me, my all-pervading Lord, and set me free.
In countless pleasures and powers, O mortal, you have forgotten (God); fallen into the world-ocean, (you take yourself to have) become immortal.
Robbed by Maya, you do not remember (God); idle, you have squandered your life.
O mortal, you must walk a hard and dreadful path, where neither sun nor moon can enter.
The love of Maya is forgotten only then, when the world is left behind.
Today it has become plain to my mind that Dharam Raj must be faced;
there the mighty ones (Death's messengers) crush (souls) with their hands; before them I cannot hold my ground.
When someone gives me teaching, then (I see) Narayan pervading the forest and every blade of grass.
Says Trilochan: O dear Ram, you yourself know everything. ॥5॥
92.2: Sri Raag, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Listen, O pandit, to one wonder; now nothing (of it) can be told.
(He) who has bewitched the gods, men, ganas and gandharvas, and girdled the three worlds (with Maya):
the harp of the Sovereign Lord plays (within me), unstruck and unbroken,
he by whose glance (of grace) the attention is held by the Naad (the Shabad).
The sky (the Tenth Gate) is my still, with its two pipes, the singia and the chungia; in the golden vat (of a pure heart) I have found the One.
Into it trickles a stream (of the nectar of the Name), utterly pure; the finest essence of all essences has been distilled.
One wondrous thing has come about: I have made (my) breath the cup.
In the three worlds the One alone is the Yogi (joined to all); tell me, who (else) is king?
Thus has the knowledge of the Supreme Being been revealed; says Kabir, I am dyed in his love.
The rest of the world, all of it, strays in delusion; (my) mind is drunk on the Lord, the home of every essence. ॥4॥
93.1: Sri Raag, the hymn of Bhagat Beni Ji; to be sung in the ghar of the Pahare.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O man, when you lay coiled in the womb, your attention was held in meditation on the Most High.
In that body of clay you had no pride in your own being; day and night (you held to) the One, and ignorance was absent.
Remember those days of hardship and great pain; now you have spread your mind far and wide (in the world's affairs).
When you left the womb and came into the mortal world, you put the Lord out of your mind.
You will regret it later, you fool; what evil counsel, what delusion, have you fallen into?
Remember the Lord, or you will go to the city of Jam; you roam about like one unbridled.
(As a child) you were taken up with childish play and thoughts of tasty things; moment by moment attachment held you.
Lured by taste, you tasted poison as if it were pure nectar; then the five (passions) began to torment you openly.
Leaving aside chanting, austerity, self-restraint and a mind set on good deeds, you did not worship the Name of the Lord.
Lust surged up and a stain fell on your intellect; then a wife was brought and tied to your neck.
In the heat of youth you eye the faces of other men's wives; you did not know a fit time from an unfit one.
Drunk with lust, astray in the deadly poison, you did not tell sin from virtue.
Seeing sons and wealth, this mind swelled with pride, and lost the Lord from the heart.
When others die, your mind weighs up their wealth; thus you have wasted this excellent birth, won by good fortune.
(In old age) the hair grows whiter than the white lotus, and the voice (grows faint) as if from the seventh underworld.
The eyes water, intellect and strength have fled, yet lust churns (within) like a churning staff.
So the intellect has become a monsoon of vices, and the lotus of the body has withered.
Having forsaken the word (of praise) of the Unknowable Lord in this mortal world, one must then repent afterwards.
Seeing the little bodies (of the grandchildren), affection wells up; he takes pride in them, but does not understand.
He craves to go on living, though his eyes see nothing.
(At last) the strength is spent, the bird of the mind flies away, and (the body) is not welcome in house or courtyard.
Says Beni: listen, O devotees, who has ever found liberation after death? ॥5॥
93.2: Sri Raag, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Between you and me, between me and you, what kind of difference is there?
Such as there is between gold and the bracelet (made of it), or water and its waves.
If we did not commit sins, O Infinite One,
how would your name be Patit Pavan, Purifier of the fallen?
You, (our) Master, are the Knower of hearts;
by the Lord the servant is known, and by the servant the Master.
Grant me understanding, that my body (while it lasts) may worship you.
May someone make Ravidas understand that (you are) the same in all. ॥3॥
